description: Classification of all 2640 WWP checklist items by distance-measurement applicability. Covers all 52 WWP guide files.

categories.horizontal: Requires plan-view distance measurement — tool CAN measure
categories.vertical-or-mixed: Requires vertical/3D clearance — tool CANNOT fully measure (yet)

subClassifications.distance-only: Distance measurement alone can resolve the verdict (compare measured value to threshold)
subClassifications.distance-plus: Distance measurement needed but verdict also requires additional information (see additionalRequirements)

additionalRequirementTypes.material-specification: Construction material type must be verified (polymer, steel, CLSM, etc.)
additionalRequirementTypes.species-verification: Tree species or root zone characteristics must be confirmed
additionalRequirementTypes.documentation-approval: Written approval or waiver from Austin Water is required
additionalRequirementTypes.access-verification: Maintenance equipment access route must be verified
additionalRequirementTypes.cleanout-specification: Cleanout type, detail, or sample port configuration must be verified
additionalRequirementTypes.surface-condition-verification: Surface type (paved, stabilized) must be verified
additionalRequirementTypes.waste-system-verification: Industrial waste or OSSF system type must be determined
additionalRequirementTypes.condition-verification: Multiple qualifying conditions must be verified
additionalRequirementTypes.system-type-verification: Water system type (reclaimed, non-potable) must be confirmed
additionalRequirementTypes.waterproofing-specification: Watertight joint specification must be verified
additionalRequirementTypes.environmental-zone-verification: Environmental zone (CWQZ, EARZ) applicability must be confirmed
additionalRequirementTypes.enclosure-specification: Security enclosure or housing specification required
additionalRequirementTypes.device-specification: Specific device type or model must be verified

WWP-1.1.deficiency: The Austin Water General Information and Construction Notes Sheet must be the current, unmodified standard template — no custom tables, removed fields, structural alterations, or modifications to any template elements

WWP-1.2.deficiency: Phase 5 water conservation tables (Domestic Meter Requirement and Irrigation Meter Requirement) must be removed from the AW General Information Sheet — these reference obsolete conservation phases no longer part of the current template

WWP-1.3.deficiency: Tables for reclaimed water or OWRS meter demand (e.g., TABLE 610.3, TABLE 103.1) must be removed from the AW General Information Sheet when no reclaimed water infrastructure or Onsite Water Reuse System is proposed

WWP-1.4.deficiency: Austin Water General Construction Notes throughout the plan set must be the current version (released February 7, 2025); all outdated or modified notes must be replaced

WWP-1.5.deficiency: Standard template field formatting must conform to the current AW template: Domestic Line Velocity field, Fire Line Velocity field, Living Unit Equivalents row labels, and Fire/Domestic/Irrigation Demand Data table structure must match the approved template format

WWP-1.6.deficiency: Inapplicable demand reduction fields on the AW template (e.g., fire flow reduction fields for IFC-based sprinkler system reductions) must be left blank when not applicable — do not enter "N/A" in these fields

WWP-1.7.deficiency: The Austin Water Infrastructure Information table must remain on the AW General Information Sheet and not be relocated to other plan sheets

WWP-1.8.deficiency: All Austin Water standard details included in the plan set must use the current revised version — outdated dated versions must be replaced with the current release; all AW standard details must be obtained directly from the City of Austin Municode site and must be legible

WWP-1.9.deficiency: Non-Austin Water content must not appear on Austin Water sheets — remove storm drainage details, watershed protection details, and lighting fixture details from AW sheets; all AW details must be on dedicated AW detail sheets, not interspersed with details from other departments

WWP-1.10.deficiency: City of Austin site plan approval blocks must appear only on cover/title sheets, not on utility detail sheets

WWP-1.11.deficiency: If no UCM waivers are being requested, the UCM Waiver Summary table must be removed from the AW General Information Sheet; all waiver information must be consolidated onto a single AW Notes sheet

WWP-1.12.deficiency: Administrative letters and correspondence (AW service availability letters, OFFSITE UTILITY LETTER blocks, placeholder Water SER Waiver letters) must not appear on plan sheets — include in the submittal package only, not on construction drawings

WWP-1.13.deficiency: Austin Water content must be placed on the correct sheets — fire flow test data and the fire flow map must appear on the AW Utility Notes Sheet, not on the cover sheet

WWP-1.14.deficiency: "Reclaimed Water" must be included in General Note 1 and throughout all general notes wherever water and wastewater are referenced together, since Austin Water operates and owns all three utility systems (water, wastewater, reclaimed water)

WWP-1.15.deficiency: Plan notes referencing the applicable plumbing code must cite the current version — notes must state that the City of Austin utilizes the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code (effective July 10, 2025, per Ord. No. 20250410-042); any reference to the 2021 Uniform Plumbing Code is outdated

WWP-1.16.deficiency: Project Information section on the AW General Notes Sheet must be complete, including building size, type, and height

WWP-1.17.deficiency: Demand data table must be fully populated with accurate GPM values for all applicable demand categories (fire, domestic, irrigation); notes beneath the table describing fire flow calculation methodology must accurately reflect UCM 2.9.2.A.3 emergency demand requirements (maximum velocity 10 fps; minimum residual pressure 20 psi at peak day plus fire flow)

WWP-1.18.deficiency: AW Infrastructure table must be populated with all proposed water and wastewater infrastructure: pipe size, material type, and linear footage

WWP-1.19.deficiency: Main extension information on the AW General Information Sheet must include length, diameter, material, connection points, and whether the extension will become part of the public system

WWP-1.20.deficiency: LUE Tracking Table must be complete with all utility easements for AW infrastructure located outside the right-of-way; LUE values must match approved Service Extension Request documentation

WWP-1.21.deficiency: All required Yes/No checkboxes on the AW General Information Sheet must be completed with "X" marks inside the checkbox boundaries

WWP-1.22.deficiency: UCC number field must be completed on the AW General Information Sheet

WWP-1.23.deficiency: Service Extension Request section must be fully completed on the AW General Information Sheet as information becomes available; if no SER is required, the section must be marked accordingly (not left blank)

WWP-1.24.deficiency: The Additional Review Acknowledgement box must be present when required (site plan submittals involving multiple Austin Water review disciplines) and absent when not required; when present, the box must contain sections for (1) Automated Metering Information, (2) AULCC Requirement, and (3) OWRS/Reclaimed Information

WWP-1.25.deficiency: Austin Water Review Block must be fully completed on the AW General Information and Construction Notes Sheet

WWP-1.26.deficiency: Inapplicable data fields must be marked "NA" rather than left blank (e.g., RECLAIMED WATER SERVICE when not proposed, STATIC PRESSURE AT HIGHEST LOT SERVED when not applicable to the project type)

WWP-1.27.deficiency: Capital Recovery Fees for meter sizes shown on the AW General Notes Sheet must be current and up to date per Austin Water fee schedules

WWP-1.28.deficiency: Meter Notice table must list all proposed water meters by type (domestic, irrigation, reclaimed, fire demand as applicable) with meter address, proposed use, type, size, GPM range, and service units

WWP-1.29.deficiency: Service Units section in the Meter Notice must include fixture count, fixture unit totals, and peak demand flows; service unit values must be correctly calculated per applicable Austin Water methodology and LDC § 25-9

WWP-1.30.deficiency: Every meter listed in the Meter Notice on the AW sheet must be illustrated on the utility plan sheets, and every meter illustrated on the utility plan sheets must be listed in the Meter Notice — bidirectional cross-check required

WWP-1.31.deficiency: Meter sizes must be consistent across all plan sheets: AW General Information Sheet, Overall Site Plan, Utility Plan, and Public Water Plan and Profile sheets

WWP-1.32.deficiency: Meter sizing sheet must be emailed to AW_ONSITEREUSE@austintexas.gov for approval, and the approved/signed sheet must be pasted into the AW Notes Sheet

WWP-1.33.deficiency: All existing water meters must be verified against Austin Water's Utility Permitting Office tap card records (size, type, and meter number) prior to plan approval

WWP-1.34.deficiency: Any existing water meter labeled "UNK" (unknown) must be located in the field and verified through Austin Water tap card records before plan approval

WWP-1.35.deficiency: Water meter numbers (including serial numbers and meter ID numbers) must not be placed on construction plan sheets — water meter numbers will not be required to be placed on the plan sheet per UCM 2.8.4.B

WWP-1.36.deficiency: Each existing water meter must have an explicitly specified disposition callout on plans: remain in service, remove and return to Austin Water, or abandon in place

WWP-1.37.deficiency: Existing water meters that will remain in service must be documented on the AW General Notes Sheet identifying the specific facility or structure each meter serves

WWP-1.38.deficiency: A "Meter Return Note" stating "Coordinate with City of Austin Inspector for meter return(s) to Austin Water" must be added to all applicable plan sheets; Construction Note 16 must also specify the Austin Water facility or inspector location for meter returns

WWP-1.39.deficiency: A separate Austin Water Taps Office form must be submitted to provide information for any abandoned water meter to receive appropriate credits

WWP-1.40.deficiency: Existing meters shown on the demolition plan must be identified with their sizes and labeled to indicate they will be collected and returned to Austin Water as City property

WWP-1.41.deficiency: Austin Water infrastructure to be abandoned, removed, or salvaged must be identified using call notes (not keyed notes)

WWP-2.23.deficiency: All proposed public water and/or wastewater easements not submitted electronically to Austin Water Pipeline Engineering (AWPE) for review, comment, and approval prior to recordation per UCM 2.9.1.A.2.

WWP-2.28.deficiency: Current Austin Water easement templates not used in preparation of easement documents per UCM 2.5.1.E.22 and AWPE standards.

WWP-2.29.deficiency: Private wastewater easements for proposed private wastewater piping on adjoining property not coordinated with Austin Water designated representative for approval and proper recordation.

WWP-2.35.deficiency: Water Service Extension Request (SER) number, project name, and Austin Water project number not documented on the plans per UCM 2.5.1.E.22 and UCM 2.5.2.A.2.

WWP-2.36.deficiency: Signed property owner acknowledgment letter not provided confirming that no Certificate of Occupancy, Temporary Certificate of Occupancy, or water meters will be released until all water infrastructure is installed, tested, and accepted by Austin Water.

WWP-2.37.deficiency: CCN release from the current utility provider not obtained prior to development plan approval for a site not within the Austin Water Utility CCN service area per 16 TAC § 24.239 and LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2). WWP-2.38.deficiency: If Southwest Water or Mid-Tex Water Utility will provide service: provider not listed as signatory on the cover page and their designated engineer has not reviewed and approved the proposed utility plan. WWP-2.39.deficiency: If Northtown MUD will be the water and/or wastewater service provider: MUD approval signature not present on the cover sheet, or documentation not provided verifying the 2006 Interlocal Agreement covers this property, or that the agreement has been amended accordingly. WWP-2.40.deficiency: Signed property owner letter not provided acknowledging that water meters, Certificates of Occupancy, and Temporary Certificates of Occupancy will not be issued until the off-site improvements shown on the Water Service Extension Request (SER) and Wastewater Service Extension Request (WWSER) are completed and accepted by Austin Water.

WWP-2.41.deficiency: When Engineering Summary Letter or concept plan states the site does not require water or wastewater tie-in or utility services: formal documentation from Austin Water confirming this determination not provided.

WWP-2.43.deficiency: Letter of Understanding from property owner not provided before Austin Water plan sign-off when utilities are still pending approval and GIS asset numbers have not yet been assigned.

WWP-2.44.deficiency: Current Austin Water Utility service area map showing the project site and service area boundaries not provided or previously submitted map is outdated.

WWP-2.45.deficiency: Project water supply demands — domestic, irrigation, and fire flow — not provided for Austin Water evaluation of whether existing water infrastructure can meet required demands within allowable pressures and velocities.

WWP-2.46.deficiency: Hydraulic analysis for proposed water lines not provided in accordance with Austin Water Utility Standard Specifications.

WWP-2.47.deficiency: Austin Water Pressure Calculator (COA Operations Webmap) not used to calculate design pressures to verify compliance with actual system configuration and current pressure zone parameters.

WWP-2.48.deficiency: If project proposes to connect to a water main that is not yet constructed: pressure information from Austin Water or independent hydraulic analysis for the design not provided.

WWP-2.49.deficiency: Utility phasing plan not provided demonstrating that fire hydrant water supply will remain operational throughout construction, for a site that is dependent on a separate Service Extension Request that is not yet complete per City of Austin Fire Criteria Manual §§ 501.3, 503, and 507.

WWP-12.50.deficiency: Typical cross sections showing multiple utilities proposed within private streets or easements are not provided on the plan set

WWP-12.51.deficiency: The design of retaining walls, bridges, culverts, headwalls, junction structures, screening walls, or stormwater drainage pipe in the vicinity of AW utilities does not demonstrate compliance with TCM Section 13 as required by UCM 2.9.1.E; or clearance dimensions from wastewater service pipes to structural elements (retaining wall footings, edges) are not dimensioned on the plans

WWP-13.1.deficiency: No manhole provided at an intersection of wastewater mains.

WWP-13.2.deficiency: No manhole provided at a horizontal alignment change (bend) in a wastewater main.

WWP-13.3.deficiency: No manhole provided at a vertical alignment change (grade change) in a wastewater main.

WWP-13.4.deficiency: No manhole provided at a change in wastewater pipe size.

WWP-13.5.deficiency: No manhole provided at a change in wastewater pipe material.

WWP-13.6.deficiency: No manhole provided at the upstream terminus of a public wastewater main.

WWP-13.7.deficiency: Cleanout used instead of manhole at a horizontal deflection in a wastewater service line.

WWP-13.8.deficiency: No manhole provided at the point of discharge of a force main into a gravity wastewater main.

WWP-13.9.deficiency: Storm drain system missing a manhole at a required location per DCM 5.6.1: pipe intersection, alignment change, pipe size change, or location where two or more laterals intersect within five feet of each other.

WWP-13.10.deficiency: Public manhole not provided at the transition point from a private to a public storm drain system.

WWP-13.11.deficiency: Public manhole at the private-to-public storm drain transition is not located within public ROW or a drainage easement.

WWP-13.12.deficiency: Manhole (not cleanout) not provided on the wastewater main at the service connection for a multi-family development exceeding 15 dwelling units.

WWP-13.13.deficiency: Manhole (not cleanout) not provided on the wastewater main at the service connection for a commercial development with more than 4,000 SF of air-conditioned space requiring a water meter greater than 2 inches. Both the square footage AND meter size conditions must be satisfied; a project over 4,000 SF AC with a ≤2-inch meter does not trigger this requirement.

WWP-13.14.deficiency: Wastewater service connection made directly to a main greater than 15 inches in diameter (no service connections are permitted to mains larger than 15 inches).

WWP-13.15.deficiency: Private manhole not shown between the curb line and property line to clearly delineate the transition from private to public wastewater infrastructure.

WWP-13.16.deficiency: Service lateral inlet not positioned within the rear one-third of the manhole perimeter relative to the main flow direction.

WWP-13.17.deficiency: Wastewater manhole spacing exceeds the 500-foot maximum for pipes smaller than 24 inches in diameter.

WWP-13.18.deficiency: Storm drain access point spacing exceeds the 250-foot maximum for pipes 30 inches or smaller in diameter. Access points include qualifying manholes, outfalls (accessible per DCM 1.2.4, single-bend maintenance path), and inlets (upstream terminus only, <250 ft from downstream manhole, colinear manhole cover).

WWP-13.19.deficiency: Storm drain access point spacing exceeds the 300-foot maximum for pipes greater than 30 inches in diameter.

WWP-13.20.deficiency: An inlet or outfall is used as a storm drain access point in lieu of a manhole, but does not satisfy all qualifying conditions per DCM 5.6.1. Outfalls must be accessible per DCM 1.2.4. Inlets must be: (1) the upstream terminus of the storm drain system, (2) located less than 250 feet from a downstream manhole, and (3) have a manhole cover colinear with the connecting pipe.

WWP-13.21.deficiency: Linear distance between manholes or access points not dimensioned on plans, preventing verification of maximum spacing compliance.

WWP-13.22.deficiency: Manhole located within a sidewalk or trail, obstructing maintenance equipment access.

WWP-13.23.deficiency: Manhole located within ROW, curb, or gutter area, preventing access by maintenance equipment.

WWP-13.24.deficiency: Manhole located in a drainage low point where surface runoff could drain into or submerge the structure.

WWP-13.25.deficiency: Manhole access is not provided at a property line or ROW connection point for storm drain systems, preventing public and private maintenance.

WWP-13.26.deficiency: All-weather access road for a manhole not accessible from an existing improved road does not meet the required design criteria: minimum 12-foot width within a 20-foot access easement; maximum 15% longitudinal slope; maximum 5% transverse slope; maximum 12% vertical grade break; minimum 14-foot horizontal and vertical clearance from vegetation and other objects; stabilization per Standard Detail 662S-2. Turnaround must be provided when the access road is more than 200 feet from a paved public road (mandatory requirement). Minimum inside turning radius of 28.3 feet and outside turning radius of 42 feet are advisory design targets.

WWP-13.27.deficiency: Manhole not accessible to required maintenance equipment: vacuum trucks, backhoes, loaders, and 2½-ton trucks, due to physical site constraints.

WWP-13.28.deficiency: Manhole cover not set flush with the finished surface elevation.

WWP-13.29.deficiency: Wastewater manhole minimum depth of cover is insufficient: less than 42 inches in easements or undeveloped areas, or less than 66 inches in streets or traffic areas.

WWP-13.30.deficiency: Wastewater manhole serving mains up to 15 inches in diameter at depths less than 20 feet does not have a minimum 48-inch inside diameter.

WWP-13.31.deficiency: Wastewater manhole serving mains 18–24 inches in diameter at depths less than 20 feet does not have a minimum 60-inch inside diameter.

WWP-13.32.deficiency: Wastewater manhole at depths between 20 and 30 feet does not have a minimum 60-inch inside diameter.

WWP-13.33.deficiency: Wastewater manhole at depths greater than 30 feet does not have a minimum 72-inch inside diameter.

WWP-13.34.deficiency: Manhole diameter not increased beyond the standard minimum to accommodate more than two connecting mains or connections at angles other than 180 degrees (larger diameter needed for mandrel insertion and hydraulic efficiency).

WWP-13.35.deficiency: Splitter box does not include a minimum 32-inch manhole per COA Standard Detail 503S-4S.

WWP-13.36.deficiency: Manhole cut sheets not submitted to Austin Water Pipeline Engineering for review and approval for manholes larger than 48 inches in diameter. Plans show a 60-inch or 72-inch precast manhole without a reference to AW Pipeline Engineering review or a separate shop drawing submittal.

WWP-13.37.deficiency: Manholes not clearly labeled as existing or proposed on plans.

WWP-13.38.deficiency: Manhole inside diameter (size) not labeled for existing or proposed manholes.

WWP-13.39.deficiency: Manhole type (e.g., drop manhole, standard manhole) not labeled on plans.

WWP-13.40.deficiency: Manhole material not labeled on plans.

WWP-13.41.deficiency: Rim elevation not labeled on plan view or profile for manholes.

WWP-13.42.deficiency: Invert/flowline elevations not labeled with "IN" and "OUT" designations for each pipe connection at manholes.

WWP-13.43.deficiency: Pipe sizes for all incoming and outgoing lines not called out in manhole labels or callouts.

WWP-13.44.deficiency: Flow direction arrows missing at pipe connections in manhole plan view or invert details.

WWP-13.45.deficiency: Incorrect utility-type symbol used for manhole (e.g., wastewater symbol used for storm drain manhole or vice versa), or symbol does not match the current City of Austin standard symbol for the utility type.

WWP-13.46.deficiency: Legend entry for manhole type does not match current COA naming convention (e.g., "PROPOSED SANITARY MANHOLE" must read "WW MH").

WWP-13.47.deficiency: Station numbers on manhole invert details do not match the corresponding manholes shown on the plan view.

WWP-13.48.deficiency: Manhole identification numbers not verified as correct, or manhole structures not confirmed to be in their correct geographic location relative to utility records.

WWP-13.49.deficiency: Manhole detail drawings not provided or not included in the construction document set.

WWP-13.50.deficiency: Manhole adjustment or detail drawings not provided at the required minimum scale (1" = 10' minimum).

WWP-13.51.deficiency: Manhole detail drawings not rotated to match plan view orientation and compass direction.

WWP-13.52.deficiency: Manhole detail drawings do not accurately depict the correct pipe sizes, materials, and configurations consistent with the plan view.

WWP-13.53.deficiency: When adjusting an existing manhole to match finished surface elevation, the new ring and cover size is not shown in the adjustment detail.

WWP-13.54.deficiency: Base type (cast-in-place vs. precast) not specified for each proposed manhole.

WWP-13.55.deficiency: Manhole not constructed by the permit applicant (i.e., constructed by others) is not identified with the project name, AW project number, and SER number on the plans.

WWP-13.56.deficiency: Flush frame and cover installation detail not provided when a manhole frame/cover is placed within a public sidewalk.

WWP-14.1.deficiency: Wastewater service lines 4–6 inches in diameter must use a COA-approved two-way cleanout — Standard Detail 520-AW-01C on the public side of the property line in public ROW or utility easement; AW-SPECIAL-04 or AW-SPECIAL-07 on the private side (verify current validity of AW-SPECIAL details with Austin Water)

WWP-14.2.deficiency: Wastewater service lines 8–12 inches in diameter must use a large diameter cleanout (LDCO) per Standard Detail 506-AW-04 — the obsolete detail 506S-14 is not acceptable

WWP-14.3.deficiency: The two-way cleanout must be a single-riser configuration with visible flow through the fitting — a "double cleanout" (two risers with concealed flow) is not an acceptable substitute; the correct configuration is governed by Standard Detail 520-AW-01C

WWP-14.4.deficiency: Horizontal alignment changes in wastewater mains require a manhole, not a cleanout — cleanouts may only be placed on straight pipe runs

WWP-14.5.deficiency: Dead-end wastewater mains must terminate at the upstream end with a manhole, not a cleanout

WWP-14.6.deficiency: The wastewater service line cleanout must be located at or near the property line within public ROW or utility easement, establishing the maintenance responsibility boundary between Austin Water and the property owner — for lots without a 5 ft × 5 ft water/wastewater easement, the cleanout terminates at the property line; for lots with a 5×5 easement, the cleanout terminates within that easement

WWP-14.7.deficiency: For an LDCO at the property line transition, the bend fitting must occur on the private side; only one flow line may enter on the City/public side of the ROW or property line

WWP-14.8.deficiency: Plans must clearly designate whether each cleanout serves public or private infrastructure to establish maintenance responsibility — unlabeled cleanouts near the property line are not acceptable

WWP-14.9.deficiency: Only one cleanout is required at the property line terminus — redundant cleanouts at the same property line location must be removed; on lots with a 5 ft × 5 ft water/wastewater easement, one cleanout within the easement satisfies the requirement

WWP-14.10.deficiency: Wastewater cleanouts must not be located in sidewalks, paved areas, load-bearing pavement, or driveways — these are the four expressly prohibited categories under UCM 2.9.4.G.6; vehicle traffic areas and parking areas are prohibited equivalently as "paved areas"

WWP-14.11.deficiency: Cleanouts must be accessible at grade — not placed in raised planters, elevated areas, or positions blocked by walls, structures, or overhead obstructions

WWP-14.12.deficiency: Where a wastewater line runs beneath or through a paved, traffic, or parking area that would prevent accessible cleanout placement, the line must be relocated to allow cleanout installation in a non-prohibited area; if a Standard Detail 520-AW-03 frame and lid arrangement is used to protect the cleanout at grade, confirm the cleanout is outside the prohibited zone — the frame detail does not authorize cleanout placement in prohibited areas

WWP-14.13.deficiency: Plans must label the cleanout placement area in sufficient detail — showing surrounding pavement edges, curb lines, and driveway boundaries near each cleanout symbol — to allow a reviewer to verify cleanouts are not in prohibited zones

WWP-14.14.deficiency: LDCO depth must not exceed 14 feet from rim to base (invert) — if depth would exceed 14 feet, an alternate structure (typically a manhole) is required instead of an LDCO

WWP-14.15.deficiency: Rim elevation and flowline (invert) elevation must be shown on both plan view and profile view for all LDCOs — without both elevations, depth compliance cannot be verified and the plans are deficient

WWP-14.16.deficiency: Pipe must run straight (180°) through the cleanout structure — no angular offsets, bends, or deflections are permitted within the cleanout body; the correct configuration is prescribed by Standard Details 520-AW-01C (two-way cleanout) and 506-AW-04 (LDCO); a plan that cites the correct detail but then shows a non-conforming profile with a deflection within the cleanout body is a deficiency

WWP-14.17.deficiency: The cleanout must maintain a constant invert elevation from inlet to outlet — vertical drops or elevation changes through the cleanout body are not permitted; both Standard Details (520-AW-01C and 506-AW-04) prescribe a straight-through, constant-invert configuration

WWP-14.18.deficiency: Linear footage between the upstream wastewater manhole and the cleanout must be annotated to verify that the minimum 1% pipe grade requirement is achievable — without distance annotation alongside elevation labels, grade cannot be confirmed

WWP-14.19.deficiency: Grade breaks along wastewater service lines must be made with approved fittings and the cumulative total of all grade breaks must not exceed 45 degrees — this is a separate and lower threshold than the UPC § 719.1 cleanout-triggering threshold of 135° cumulative horizontal direction change

WWP-14.20.deficiency: Minimum 5-foot horizontal separation (measured OD to OD) must be maintained between wastewater cleanouts and storm sewer infrastructure — the residential exception (3 ft allowed between water, reclaimed water, and wastewater service lines and dry utility service lines) does not apply to storm sewer

WWP-14.21.deficiency: Cleanout must not be installed at a wye (Y) intersection — install the cleanout just downstream of the intersection on a straight run; a cleanout at a wye is a structural and maintenance access deficiency

WWP-14.22.deficiency: Drop connections are permitted only in manholes, not in cleanout structures — a service line connecting to a cleanout with a vertical drop (inlet invert above outlet invert, with the elevation change occurring inside the cleanout body) is not acceptable; cleanouts are configured as straight-through structures per Standard Details 520-AW-01C and 506-AW-04; any vertical elevation change at a connection point must be routed through a manhole where crown-to-crown matching is required (or AW UDS approval obtained for deviation)

WWP-14.23.deficiency: Cleanouts must be installed at intervals not exceeding 100 feet on straight gravity wastewater service line runs

WWP-14.24.deficiency: A cleanout is required at each location where the aggregate horizontal direction change in the wastewater service line exceeds 135° — this is the UPC § 719.1 threshold; the separate UCM 2.9.4.G.2 cumulative 45° grade break limit applies to fittings, not to cleanout placement

WWP-14.25.deficiency: A cleanout is required at all vertical bends in wastewater service lines

WWP-14.26.deficiency: A cleanout is required immediately downstream of each point where separate wastewater streams combine (e.g., grease trap effluent combining with a sanitary drain line) — this captures combined flow for inspection and cleaning access at each junction

WWP-14.27.deficiency: A cleanout is required at dead-end service line termini for maintenance flushing and inspection access

WWP-14.28.deficiency: Force main cleanout spacing must meet Austin Water administrative standards: single cleanouts at approximately 500-foot intervals; dual (two-way) cleanouts at approximately 950–1,000-foot intervals; force mains smaller than 4 inches in diameter at ≤150-foot intervals — these values are Austin Water operational standards; if plans do not confirm compliance, verify directly with Austin Water Pipeline Engineering

WWP-14.29.deficiency: Force main cleanout spacing must ensure cumulative bends between consecutive cleanouts do not exceed 180° total — cleaning equipment cannot navigate beyond this cumulative bend limit

WWP-14.30.deficiency: Force main profile must show all cleanout locations and their spacing dimensions

WWP-14.31.deficiency: Private force main cleanout assembly must consist of a wye fitting, shutoff valve, and plug — standard gravity cleanout box structures (e.g., SD 520-AW-01C) are not acceptable on pressurized force main segments

WWP-14.32.deficiency: At the private-to-public force main transition, plans must show all three required elements: (a) a public cleanout at the property line per UCM 2.9.4.G.5; (b) a polymer discharge manhole for the force main discharge per UCM 2.9.4.J.7.g — multiple force mains cannot share a single polymer manhole; and (c) a manhole on the existing gravity main at the force main discharge point per UCM 2.9.4.D.1.f, with a short gravity segment between manholes; plans missing any of these elements at the transition are deficient

WWP-14.33.deficiency: A COA-approved two-way cleanout or LDCO serving as a sampling and inspection port must be installed for compliance with § 15-10-226 industrial waste monitoring requirements for any commercial, institutional, industrial, food service, hotel, medical, laboratory, governmental, or similar non-residential use that discharges to the sanitary sewer — single-family residences and duplexes are exempt

WWP-14.34.deficiency: The sampling and inspection port must reference a currently active standard detail — for laterals ≤6 inches: SD 520-AW-01C or SD 520-AW-03; for 8–12 inch laterals: SD 506-AW-04; plans citing obsolete details (506S-14, 520-AW-01, 520S-3A) are deficient; AW-SPECIAL details (AW-SPECIAL-07, etc.) require confirmation from Austin Water that the cited special detail number remains current and approved

WWP-14.35.deficiency: Plans must clearly distinguish between two-way cleanouts installed for maintenance access only (UCM 2.9.4.G.5) and sample ports installed for industrial waste monitoring (UCM 2.9.4.G.7) — each must be separately labeled with its function; where a single structure serves both purposes (authorized under § 15-10-227 with director approval), that dual function must be explicitly labeled

WWP-14.36.deficiency: Sample port must be located downstream of ALL wastewater stream confluences for the building or metered group — including sanitary drains, grease trap effluent, floor drains, and all process streams — and before that building's or meter group's total combined flow joins wastewater from any other building, structure, or separately metered area; a sample port positioned between any two confluence points does not capture representative composite discharge

WWP-14.37.deficiency: For sites with more than one drain line connected to the sanitary sewer, a dedicated sample port must be installed on each drain line before that line's flow combines with any other drain line — the code trigger is the number of drain lines (§ 15-10-226(D)(2)), not the number of water meters; in practice, each domestic water meter's wastewater service is typically a separate drain line, but a site could have separate drain lines from a single meter or combined drain lines from multiple meters

WWP-14.38.deficiency: Sample wells located immediately downstream of a grease trap alone are not acceptable as COA sample port locations — a sample well at the grease trap outlet captures only grease trap effluent, not the full building wastewater stream; the sample port must be downstream of all wastewater confluences, including sanitary drain lines; if a sample well is shown only at the grease trap, it must be removed or relocated

WWP-14.39.deficiency: For private lift stations, a two-way cleanout sample port must be installed immediately upstream of the lift station on the gravity portion of the service line, before the wastewater enters the lift station wet well — sample ports must be on gravity segments to capture representative samples

WWP-14.40.deficiency: Sample port must not be placed on a force main section or downstream of a lift station — pressurized flow and batch discharge from a pump prevent collection of representative grab samples; the sample port must be on a gravity portion of the wastewater line

WWP-14.41.deficiency: Sample port must not be located in vehicle traffic areas, parking areas, driveways, sidewalks, or load-bearing pavement — the UCM 2.9.4.G.7 prohibited zone list for sample ports includes "traffic areas, paved parking areas or sidewalks"

WWP-14.42.deficiency: Sample port must be located at or near the property line or edge of the wastewater easement, on the public side, in a non-traffic, non-parking area — for lots with a 5 ft × 5 ft water/wastewater easement, location within the easement is compliant

WWP-14.43.deficiency: Sample port must be accessible at all times with fully unobstructed access for Austin Water Industrial Waste personnel to hang sampling equipment safely below surface level — the port must not be blocked by walls, structures, pedestrian pathways, or overhead obstructions

WWP-14.44.deficiency: Where a force main transitions to a gravity wastewater line at a manhole, that transition manhole may serve as the COA sample port only if and only if it is in a non-traffic, non-parking area — this requires express director approval under § 15-10-227

WWP-14.45.deficiency: Sample port must be labeled on plans as "Sample Port with 2-way cleanout" (or equivalent approved phrasing) and must reference the applicable standard detail number — labels showing only "2-way cleanout" or "cleanout" without the "Sample Port" designation are insufficient

WWP-14.46.deficiency: Sample port inlet (influent) and outlet (effluent) piping must be clearly labeled on plans to indicate flow direction

WWP-14.47.deficiency: Sample port must be shown on the wastewater profile drawing in addition to the plan view — profile view must show the sample port symbol, label, and elevation data

WWP-14.48.deficiency: Elevator sump pump discharge piping must remain separate from all other building piping until it connects to a dedicated sample port; the sample port must be located outside the building footprint (or inside the building for zero-lot-line conditions, or as approved by the director), and must be shown and labeled on plans

WWP-14.49.deficiency: School facility wastewater sample ports must have a Hotbox LB3000 (or COA-approved equivalent) security enclosure installed over the sample port cleanout — the enclosure must be located inside the school's fenced area; if interior installation is infeasible, the enclosure may be placed within 5 feet outside the fenced area; this is an Austin Water administrative standard implemented under the director's approval authority; plans for school projects that do not show the Hotbox LB3000 or equivalent security enclosure with location relative to the fenced area are deficient

WWP-14.50.deficiency: Each cleanout must be labeled on plans with correct type terminology and the applicable standard detail reference number — e.g., "2-way cleanout per SD 520-AW-01C" or "large diameter cleanout per SD 506-AW-04" — generic labels such as "12" CLEANOUT," "double cleanout," or cleanout symbols without a detail citation are not acceptable

WWP-14.51.deficiency: Rim elevation and flowline (invert) elevation must be labeled for all cleanouts on plans — not just for LDCOs — so that grade, depth, and elevation continuity through the structure can be verified

WWP-14.52.deficiency: Cleanouts must be shown on both the plan view and the wastewater profile view, including depth, connection configuration, and fitting details — a cleanout appearing on the plan view but omitted from the profile (or vice versa) is a documentation deficiency

WWP-14.53.deficiency: All cleanout callout labels must have leader lines pointing to the actual cleanout symbol on the plans — labels with leaders pointing to adjacent pipe runs, surrounding pavement, or blank areas are not acceptable and prevent verification of cleanout location and type

WWP-14.54.deficiency: Cleanouts must be labeled with station numbers and GIS numbers on the plan view — generic type labels alone are not sufficient; UCM 2.5.3.A.4 specifically requires station numbers and GIS numbers for cleanouts along with other appurtenances; absence of these identifiers prevents GIS record maintenance and field verification

WWP-14.55.deficiency: Profile view must include station numbers and elevations at each cleanout location — UCM 2.5.3.B.5 requires station numbers and elevations for cleanouts on the profile view, in addition to the starting and ending points and intermediate points every 100 feet; a profile showing cleanout elevation labels but lacking station annotation is deficient

WWP-14.56.deficiency: Air release valve cleanout details must be included on the wastewater detail sheets — where air release valves are proposed on wastewater lines, the associated cleanout assembly must be detailed showing the configuration, standard detail reference, and connection to the wastewater main

WWP-14.57.deficiency: Existing cleanouts proposed to be retained must comply with current COA standard details — if a retained cleanout references an obsolete detail (506S-14, 520-AW-01, 520S-3A, or others), the cleanout must be replaced with a new compliant cleanout conforming to the current applicable standard detail

WWP-14.58.deficiency: Each LDCO must have a security enclosure (Hotbox LB3000 or COA-approved equivalent) shown on plans to prevent vandalism and damage by maintenance vehicles — the enclosure must be called out on both the utility plan and detail sheet

WWP-14.59.deficiency: Exposed cleanout piping must be avoided or minimized — where exposed piping is unavoidable, a protective enclosure must be provided; plans showing exposed riser piping above grade without a protective enclosure callout are deficient

WWP-14.60.deficiency: Cleanout connections accessible to food trailers must include a locking mechanism to prevent unauthorized access and cross-connection — plans for food trailer hookup areas must show a locking cap or equivalent security device on each cleanout within the hookup zone

WWP-15.1.deficiency: Public wastewater gravity main does not meet minimum 8-inch inside diameter.

WWP-15.2.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main is specified in a non-standard diameter; only allowable sizes (8", 12", 15", 18", 24", 30", 36", 42") are permitted for gravity mains.

WWP-15.3.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main includes a diameter reduction along the pipe run; reductions in wastewater main diameter are prohibited.

WWP-15.4.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main does not maintain minimum 0.5% slope for 8-inch pipe.

WWP-15.5.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main segment has an uphill or inverted slope; gravity wastewater piping must slope continuously downhill in the direction of flow.

WWP-15.6.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main slope exceeds the TCEQ 30 TAC § 217.53 maximum slope limit for the specified pipe diameter.

WWP-15.7.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main does not achieve minimum 2 fps velocity at peak dry weather flow (PDWF).

WWP-15.8.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main velocity exceeds maximum 10 fps at peak wet weather flow (PWWF).

WWP-15.9.deficiency: PDWF exceeds 65% of full pipe flow capacity for a gravity main 15 inches or smaller in diameter; pipe is undersized for design flows.

WWP-15.10.deficiency: PWWF exceeds 85% of full pipe flow capacity for a gravity main 15 inches or smaller in diameter; pipe is undersized for design flows.

WWP-15.11.deficiency: PWWF exceeds 80% of full pipe flow capacity for a gravity main 18 inches or larger in diameter; pipe is undersized for design flows. The 80% threshold applies to all mains ≥18 inches and is stricter than the 85% threshold applicable to smaller mains — applying the 85% threshold to an 18-inch main is a violation.

WWP-15.12.deficiency: When minimum 2 fps at PDWF cannot be achieved at 0.5% slope, minimum slope has not been increased to 1.0% (0.01 ft/ft) as required by the exception.

WWP-15.13.deficiency: When minimum 2 fps at PDWF cannot be achieved, written substantiation to Austin Water explaining why 2 fps is not feasible has not been provided. Both the written substantiation (B.3.a) and the 1.0% minimum slope (B.3.b) are required simultaneously; the slope increase alone is insufficient.

WWP-15.14.deficiency: Wastewater pipe slopes (as a percentage or inches of fall per foot) are not labeled on wastewater plan/profile sheets.

WWP-15.15.deficiency: Utility plans do not clearly establish whether each wastewater pipe segment is a gravity main or a force main; this classification determines applicable slope, sizing, velocity, and discharge criteria under UCM 2.9.4.

WWP-15.16.deficiency: Wastewater pipe slopes shown on utility plans, plan/profile sheets, and the engineering report are inconsistent; values must be reconciled across all documents.

WWP-15.17.deficiency: A negative (reverse) slope is shown on a gravity wastewater pipe segment without explanation; negative slopes on gravity lines must be corrected or formally justified. Look for profile sheets where stated slope percentage is negative or where downstream invert elevations are higher than upstream inverts.

WWP-15.18.deficiency: Flow direction arrows are not provided on wastewater utility plans, preventing verification of minimum velocity and slope requirements. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.10, the direction of flow in wastewater mains must be indicated on the drawings.

WWP-15.19.deficiency: Peak flow rates (PDWF and PWWF) and calculated velocities are not documented for pipe segments between manholes on profile sheets.

WWP-15.20.deficiency: Wastewater service line does not meet minimum 6-inch inside diameter.

WWP-15.21.deficiency: Wastewater service line does not maintain minimum 1% grade (slope).

WWP-15.22.deficiency: Rim and flow-line (invert) elevations at cleanouts are not shown or do not confirm that minimum 1% service line grade is maintained throughout.

WWP-15.23.deficiency: Force main / lift station discharge piping velocity is not within the required 3–6 fps range at the design pump rate. For lift stations with 3 or more pumps during initial development, velocities as low as 2.5 fps with one pump running are acceptable; velocities between 4 and 6 fps require Austin Water case-by-case approval; velocities above 6 fps are not permitted.

WWP-15.24.deficiency: Force main / lift station discharge piping velocity has not been calculated and demonstrated at both initial and ultimate development conditions; the design must show compliance at both stages.

WWP-15.25.deficiency: Force main diameter is less than the minimum 4-inch requirement.

WWP-15.26.deficiency: Force main hydraulic report does not include headloss calculations and pipe diameter justification demonstrating velocity within the 3–6 fps range at both initial and ultimate development conditions. Velocity numbers shown on plan sheets as a single plan note, without supporting calculations, are insufficient.

WWP-15.27.deficiency: Force main is not laid at the TCEQ 30 TAC § 217.53 minimum slope requirement.

WWP-15.28.deficiency: Engineering Report does not include justification that a gravity wastewater system is not feasible, or does not include a 30-year cost-benefit analysis comparing gravity service versus lift station, as required before design begins.

WWP-15.29.deficiency: Private 4-inch or 6-inch wastewater piping does not meet minimum 2.0% slope.

WWP-15.30.deficiency: Private 8-inch wastewater piping does not meet minimum 0.5% slope per the UPC exception for larger diameters.

WWP-15.31.deficiency: Private 4-inch or 6-inch wastewater piping is shown at a reduced slope (below 2.0% but not less than 1.0%) without documented AHJ (Austin Water) approval; approval is required when the depth of the public sewer, structural features, or building arrangement prevents the standard slope.

WWP-15.32.deficiency: Private wastewater piping is not sized per UPC Tables 703.2 and 717.1 based on the drainage fixture unit (DFU) loading for the fixtures served. Austin adopts the UPC; DFU values from IPC tables are non-compliant. Both undersized pipe (exceeds DFU capacity) and oversized pipe (falls below the minimum DFU threshold required to maintain solids-transport velocity) are violations.

WWP-19.1.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead line length exceeds 55 feet; lead line length must be documented and labeled on plans to allow verification. If the lead exceeds 55 feet and no UCM § 2.9.6 Waiver Request has been submitted in writing and approved by Austin Water, issue a comment.

WWP-19.2.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead line is not 6-inch diameter. Austin Water permits only 6-inch pipe for fire hydrant leads; no other diameter is acceptable for this use.

WWP-19.3.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead line piping volume exceeds 100 gallons. Under IFC § 507.6, a hydrant lead volume exceeding 100 gallons requires backflow protection per Chapter 15-1. However, installing a backflow preventer on a hydrant lead is prohibited by NFPA 24 (adopted via LDC § 25-12-153, § 609.13 and the FPCM). The only compliant resolution is to reconfigure the piping so the lead volume is below 100 gallons — by shortening the lead or reducing its diameter. Estimate lead volume as: π × r² × L × 7.48 (r = internal pipe radius in feet; L = lead length in feet).

WWP-19.4.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead connection or assembly cannot achieve a bury length between 4 feet (48 inches) minimum and 5 feet maximum below the proposed ground elevation. SSM Item No. 511.3.E specifies this bury length for the hydrant assembly; SSM Item No. 511.4.B confirms that the lower barrel length shall not exceed 5 feet and that barrel extensions are not permitted without Engineer approval. Where the distribution main is deeper than 5 feet, the lead must be elbowed up from the main using restrained joints. Plans that show a direct connection to a pipe section at a depth that would require a barrel extension beyond 5 feet are non-compliant.

WWP-19.5.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead line crosses a lot line; private infrastructure shall not be routed across property boundaries.

WWP-19.6.deficiency: Fire hydrant lead line crosses a divided road or highway. A divided road is defined at UCM 2.9.2.B.2 as one where opposing lanes of vehicular traffic are currently or planned to be separated by a median, railroad tracks, or other vehicle obstruction. Lead lines may not cross a divided road regardless of length; water mains must be installed on both sides of the divided road to serve each side independently.

WWP-19.7.deficiency: No resilient-seated gate valve with bolt-through restraint to the distribution main is shown on the fire hydrant lead. UCM 2.9.2.C.1 requires a gate valve on each fire hydrant lead, restrained to the main using bolt-through connections between the valve and the branch outlet from the main. SSM Item No. 511.4.B also requires a 6-inch gate valve on each lead for individual shutoff.

WWP-19.8.deficiency: Fire hydrant is proposed on a water distribution main smaller than 8 inches in diameter. UCM 2.9.2.A.4 requires a minimum 8-inch nominal main for fire hydrant connections. 6-inch pipe is limited to hydrant leads and individual services, not distribution mains from which hydrants are fed.

WWP-19.9.deficiency: Fire flow capacity from the proposed main connection is not demonstrated as adequate. UCM 2.9.2.A.3 requires a maximum velocity of 10 fps and minimum residual pressure of 20 psi at any system point under peak day demand plus fire flow. Non-compliance appears as: plans proposing a connection to an undersized or remote existing main with no SER or fire flow analysis on file, or a fire flow analysis that references a different main connection than what is shown on the utility plans.

WWP-19.10.deficiency: Distribution main pipe size is reduced at or before the fire hydrant connection. Main size must be maintained through the hydrant tee before any downstream size reduction to preserve fire flow capacity; a reduction upstream of the hydrant tee reduces available flow and pressure.

WWP-19.11.deficiency: Dead-end water main does not have a fire hydrant at or near the terminus equipped with an automatic flushing device to achieve 72-hour water turnover per UCM 2.9.2.B.1.b. An automatic flushing device is required until active demand from the system achieves adequate turnover.

WWP-19.12.deficiency: Dead-end water main does not include a gate valve near the end followed by one joint of restrained pipe (of engineer-determined length adequate for future extension) and a plug with a 1-inch or larger tap per UCM 2.9.2.B.1.a. The engineer must determine the necessary length of pipe restraint on each side of the valve to keep the main in place when the plug is removed for future extension. No services are permitted between the gate valve and the plug.

WWP-19.13.deficiency: Fire hydrant is designed to be within 9 feet in any direction of a wastewater main, lateral, or service. UCM 2.9.2.D.4 prohibits this regardless of the material of construction of either pipe.

WWP-19.14.deficiency: Fire hydrant steamer outlet (4-inch pumper nozzle) center is not located approximately 18 inches above finished grade per SSM Item No. 511.3.E and SSM Item No. 511.4.B.

WWP-19.15.deficiency: Fire hydrant burial depth (bury length from finished ground elevation to the lead pipe connection) is less than 4 feet (48 inches) or greater than 5 feet below the proposed ground elevation per SSM Item No. 511.3.E. Barrel extensions are not permitted without Engineer approval (SSM Item No. 511.4.B).

WWP-19.16.deficiency: Fire hydrant is not specified to be installed plumb per SSM Item No. 511.4.B. Where hydrants are located near curbs, the 4-inch pumper nozzle shall face the curb and be perpendicular to it.

Nozzles shall have stainless steel locking devices.

WWP-19.18.deficiency: Valve on the fire hydrant lead uses push-on joints; push-on joint valves are not permitted for fire hydrant leads and laterals per UCM 2.9.2.C.10.

WWP-19.19.deficiency: Plans do not include a blue Type II-B-B reflectorized pavement marker placed 2 to 3 feet offset from the centerline of the paved street on the side of and in line with each new fire hydrant per SSM Item No. 511.3.E.

WWP-19.20.deficiency: Fire hydrants are not clearly designated as "Public Fire Hydrant" or "Private Fire Hydrant" in the Keynote Legend and on utility plans. This designation determines applicable design standards, backflow requirements, pipe classification, and maintenance obligations.

WWP-19.21.deficiency: Private fire hydrant color is not consistent with City of Austin Standard Specifications Manual requirements. Under IFC § 507.5.7, all fire hydrants must be painted per the COA SSM. Private hydrants may be painted an alternate reflective color only with written approval from the fire code official; multi-colored hydrants are prohibited in all cases. Non-compliance appears as: private hydrant detail specifying the standard AW public hydrant color (per AW SPL WW-3) with no alternate-color approval documentation, or any hydrant specified in more than one color.

WWP-19.22.deficiency: Private fire hydrant is not served by a private water line. Hydrants connected directly to Austin Water public mains must be classified and operated as public infrastructure per UCM 2.9.2.D.12.

WWP-19.23.deficiency: Private fire hydrant maintenance obligation is not addressed on plans, or the maintenance note cites NFPA 24 instead of NFPA 25. IFC § 507.5.3 requires private fire service mains and hydrants to be inspected, tested, and maintained consistent with NFPA 25, the Fire Protection Criteria Manual, and AWWA Manual M-17 — including annual inspection and flow test, inspection after each operation, annual flushing, and a flow test of fire service main piping every 5 years. NFPA 24 governs installation; NFPA 25 governs maintenance.

WWP-19.24.deficiency: Water line easement or Joint Use Access Agreement (JUAE) is not provided when fire hydrants on adjacent property are used to meet hydrant coverage or spacing requirements. When a site relies on a hydrant located on another property for fire protection, the use of that hydrant must be formalized through a recorded easement or JUAE to ensure long-term access and prevent future relocation or obstruction. This requirement derives from Austin Fire Department and FPCM administrative policy rather than a specific codified IFC § 507.5.1 provision.

WWP-19.25.deficiency: Water line easement for fire hydrant infrastructure does not meet minimum width standards. UCM 2.9.1.A.1 requires easements for water infrastructure to be a minimum of 15 feet wide, or twice the depth of the infrastructure (measured from finished grade to the infrastructure flowline), whichever is greater, centered on the infrastructure. A narrower easement must be supported by engineer documentation that maintenance activities will not be hindered.

WWP-19.26.deficiency: Public fire hydrant is not completely bounded by a Public Utility Easement (PUE) that includes a minimum 3-foot clear area around the entire hydrant.

WWP-19.27.deficiency: No protective easement is established to prevent relocation or removal of a private hydrant on a neighboring property that is relied upon for fire protection coverage at the site under review.

WWP-19.28.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer is not located inside the property line per UCM 2.9.2.B.6. The BFP is a private appurtenance and must be on private property.

WWP-19.29.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer is located in a traffic area (drive aisle, travel lane, or parking stall), which is prohibited. UCM 2.9.2.B.6 requires the BFP to be accessible for City inspection; a BFP in a traffic area cannot be safely accessed and is subject to vehicle damage.

WWP-19.30.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer is located within a public easement. The BFP is a private appurtenance and cannot be installed within public utility easements.

WWP-19.31.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer location is not accessible for City inspection and maintenance per UCM 2.9.2.B.6. The BFP must allow unobstructed personnel access for inspection without entering traffic areas or easements.

WWP-19.32.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer location is not shown on utility plans.

WWP-19.33.deficiency: Looped or dual-feed fire lines do not show a backflow preventer at each connection point to the public water system. UCM 2.9.2.B.6 requires a BFP inside the property line at each point where a fire line connects to the City main; omitting a BFP at any connection allows dead-end pipe segments to exceed 100 gallons without flow detection protection.

WWP-19.34.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer size is not indicated on utility plans. The BFP size must match the downstream pipe size being served.

WWP-19.35.deficiency: Fire line backflow preventer type is not indicated using industry-standard nomenclature. Plans must call out the BFP as either "DCDA" (Double Check Detector Assembly) or "RPDA" (Reduced Pressure Detector Assembly) for underground unmetered fire lines; an unlabeled or generically labeled BFP cannot be verified for compliance.

WWP-19.36.deficiency: Underground unmetered fire line detail shows an incorrect backflow preventer assembly type. Must use a detector-type assembly — "DCDA" (Double Check Detector Assembly) or "RPDA" (Reduced Pressure Detector Assembly) — not a "DCVA" (Double Check Valve Assembly) or "RPZ" (Reduced Pressure Zone Assembly). A DCVA and RPZ lack the small bypass detector meter required by UCM 2.9.2.B.6 for unmetered underground fire lines.

WWP-19.37.deficiency: Fire line piping volume from the connection point (tee off domestic meter or main tee) to the backflow preventer exceeds 100 gallons. UCM 2.9.2.B.6 requires the flow detection device to be positioned so no more than 100 gallons are contained between the device and the main connection point. Piping must be reconfigured to meet this limit. Estimate volume using: π × r² × L × 7.48.

WWP-19.38.deficiency: Unmetered fire service line does not include an Austin Water-approved flow detection device. UCM 2.9.2.B.6 requires all unmetered fire lines to have an AW-approved flow detection device positioned so no more than 100 gallons of water are contained between the device and the connection point to the City main.

WWP-19.39.deficiency: Plans show a backflow preventer installed on a fire hydrant lead line. Installing a BFP on a hydrant lead is prohibited by NFPA 24 (as adopted through LDC § 25-12-153, § 609.13 and the Fire Protection Criteria Manual). Although IFC § 507.6 requires backflow protection when lead volume exceeds 100 gallons, this cannot be achieved by placing a BFP on the lead itself. Piping must instead be reconfigured to bring the lead volume below 100 gallons.

WWP-19.40.deficiency: Plans do not include an inset or enlarged fire line connection detail showing all required components: ductile iron pipe from the main connection to the property line, gate valve at the main connection, backflow preventer inside the property line, and flow detection device per UCM 2.9.2.B.6. UCM 2.5.1.E.21 requires supplementary special details as needed to convey design intent. Standard Detail 520S-19B or an equivalent engineer-prepared detail is expected.

WWP-19.41.deficiency: Fire line connection detail does not specify ductile iron (DI) pipe from the main connection to the property line per UCM 2.9.2.B.6.

WWP-19.42.deficiency: Fire line connection detail does not show a gate valve at the main connection per UCM 2.9.2.B.6.

WWP-19.43.deficiency: Fire service line is not shown installed at level grade (0% slope) through the meter vault. Level grade through the vault is required for proper backflow preventer operation, accurate flow measurement, and compliance with manufacturer specifications.

WWP-19.44.deficiency: Public and private fire line segments are not labeled on plan sheets and profiles. The public portion (from the main to the property line, including the gate valve at the tee) and the private portion (from the property line through the BFP and beyond) must be distinguished per UCM 2.9.2.B.6.

WWP-19.45.deficiency: Private fire line piping extends into the public right-of-way. The private fire line must remain on private property; the only portion within the ROW is the public segment (main to property line).

WWP-19.46.deficiency: Private fire line piping crosses a lot line, which is prohibited. A private fire line must remain on the private property it serves and cannot be routed across property boundaries.

WWP-19.47.deficiency: Utility corridor designations are applied to fire line backflow preventers or their downstream private piping. BFPs and downstream private appurtenances are not public utility infrastructure and cannot carry utility corridor designations.

WWP-19.48.deficiency: Pipes from a tapping valve or main connection are not labeled by intended use ("Proposed Water Service" or "Fire Line") on plans. Labeling is required because fire lines require different materials (DI pipe), valves, backflow prevention, and length limits than domestic service; an unlabeled or ambiguously labeled pipe cannot be verified for compliance.

WWP-19.49.deficiency: Fire service line length is not labeled on plans to allow verification of the 55-foot maximum per UCM 2.9.2.E.8. Linear length from the main to the meter must be dimensioned on plans.

WWP-19.50.deficiency: Standard Detail 520S-19B (Backflow Preventer on Fire Line with Master Meter) is included on plans when only fire hydrants are proposed with no dedicated fire service line. Fire hydrant leads do not require this detail; including it without a corresponding fire service line creates a misleading representation of the proposed infrastructure.

WWP-19.51.deficiency: Domestic demand does not justify a 3-inch or larger meter (domestic demand is below approximately 152 GPM per the AW General Information Sheet), but required fire flow is not provided through a separate dedicated fire line with a double check detector backflow prevention assembly per UCM 2.9.2.F.5. A fire demand meter is not permitted in this scenario. Exception: if both domestic and fire demand can be served by a 2-inch or smaller meter, a single meter may serve both.

WWP-19.52.deficiency: Plans include a dedicated fire service line but do not show evidence of City of Austin Fire Department approval. UCM 2.5.1.D requires that plans including fire lines obtain approval by both the AFD and the Development Services Department before plan approval is granted. Non-compliance appears as: a fire service line on the utility plan with no AFD stamp or approval notation, or an AFD stamp on earlier plan sheets but absent from the sheet containing the fire line.

WWP-19.53.deficiency: Plans include a note indicating "Optional Domestic Service Allowed on Fire Lines" when domestic demand does not require a 3-inch or larger meter. This note must be removed; UCM 2.9.2.F.5 requires a dedicated fire line in this scenario, and a domestic service on the fire line is not an acceptable option when demand does not meet the 3-inch meter threshold.

WWP-20.29.deficiency: DCVA (valve assembly) specified for an unmetered fire service line — unmetered fire lines require a detector-type assembly (DCDA or RPDA) with a bypass meter for flow detection, not a valve assembly

WWP-20.35.deficiency: BFP shown on plans is not required by the applicable COA Standard Detail — BFPs shown but not required by the relevant standard detail must be removed or the design revised to match the standard detail configuration

WWP-20.36.deficiency: BFP located in the public right-of-way rather than on private property. Fire line BFPs must be inside the property line per UCM 2.9.2.B.6; all containment BFPs must be immediately downstream of the City water meter per § 15-1-14(C)(33)(a)

WWP-20.37.deficiency: BFP located in a traffic area — must be relocated to a safe, accessible location outside parking, drive aisles, and travel lanes

WWP-20.38.deficiency: BFP located within public utility easement boundaries — Austin Water installation standards require BFPs to be on private property outside PUE boundaries to maintain accessibility and avoid conflicts with easement construction activity

WWP-20.39.deficiency: Plan notes specify BFP location as "at or near the property line" rather than "inside the property line" as required for fire line BFPs, or as "immediately downstream of the meter" as required for containment BFPs

WWP-20.40.deficiency: RPZ backflow preventer specified for underground, pit, or below-grade installation — RPZ assemblies have atmospheric relief vent ports and are prohibited from underground or submerged locations; additionally, all BFP assemblies must have minimum 12-inch clearance above grade

WWP-20.41.deficiency: BFP installed under a building deck or covered structure in a location that prevents required access or testing — RPZ assemblies with atmospheric vent ports are prohibited from enclosed pit or underground installations; all BFPs must remain accessible for testing

WWP-20.42.deficiency: BFP location inaccessible for City inspection — blocked by landscaping, structures, or other obstructions

WWP-20.43.deficiency: Fencing proposed around BFP does not maintain clear vehicular access for City inspection and maintenance

WWP-20.44.deficiency: Elevated BFP installation exceeding 5 feet (1,524 mm) above grade does not include a platform capable of supporting a technician — a platform is required for all BFP assemblies installed more than 5 feet above grade

WWP-20.45.deficiency: Minimum horizontal clearance not maintained adjacent to water line exiting the BFP — Austin Water installation standards derived from COA Standard Details require sufficient clearance for maintenance and testing access at the BFP outlet piping

WWP-20.46.deficiency: BFP not specified to be installed level (0% grade) — level installation is required for proper operation of double check and reduced pressure assemblies per COA Standard Details and manufacturer requirements

WWP-20.47.deficiency: Isolated valve not provided between the water meter and the BFP — an isolation valve between the meter and the backflow prevention device is required for irrigation systems and is standard practice for all service types per COA Standard Details

WWP-20.48.deficiency: Water meter and BFP installed in the same vault rather than in separate vaults for independent access — separate vaults are required per COA Standard Details and Table 15-1-14-A, Note 2

WWP-20.49.deficiency: Prior Austin Water utility approval not documented for BFP installed in a pit or vault — Table 15-1-14-A, Note 2 requires previous utility approval before installing any BFP in a pit or vault; this is distinct from the separate vault requirement

WWP-20.50.deficiency: Straight pipe runs not provided upstream and downstream of metering and backflow prevention equipment — straight runs are required for accurate flow measurement and proper hydraulic conditions

WWP-20.51.deficiency: Thermal expansion not addressed at water heaters where the BFP creates a closed potable water system — a closed system requires an expansion tank or other approved device

WWP-20.52.deficiency: BFP not shown in profile view with station number, elevation, and location relative to other utilities

WWP-20.53.deficiency: BFP not shown or labeled in Enlarged Meter Details

WWP-20.54.deficiency: Complete BFP vault detail drawings not provided — missing vault dimensions, rim elevations, pipe sizes, grades, or materials

WWP-20.55.deficiency: BFP installation callouts do not reference the applicable COA Standard Detail — each BFP callout must identify the specific COA Standard Detail that governs the installation

WWP-20.56.deficiency: COA Standard Detail type referenced does not match the actual BFP type shown on plans (e.g., 520S-19B referenced for an RPZ installation instead of 520S-19C) — the standard detail must correspond to the BFP type specified

WWP-20.57.deficiency: Manufacturer specification sheets not provided demonstrating USC FCCHR (University of Southern California Foundation for Cross-Connection Control and Hydraulic Research) approval for specified BFP models — all testable BFP assemblies must appear on the current USC FCCHR approved list

WWP-20.58.deficiency: Abandoned BFP facility not disconnected at the corporation stop with all appurtenances removed per UCM 2.8.4.B — additionally, abandoned BFPs should be labeled "abandoned" on plans per general plan documentation practice

WWP-20.59.deficiency: Austin Water director approval not obtained or documented for relocated BFP devices — City Code § 15-1-12(H) prohibits removing from use, relocating, or substituting a BFP without approval of the Austin Water director; plans showing a relocated BFP without director approval notation or documentation indicate a § 15-1-12(H) violation

WWP-20.60.deficiency: Third-party testing documentation not provided demonstrating the existing BFP meets current specifications when required by Austin Water for retained or reused BFPs
