WWP-22.14.deficiency: Water meter schedule or meter notice not provided, or existing schedule does not list all meters with their sizes, types, and serving connections consistent with the utility plan

WWP-22.15.deficiency: Each water meter not identified with the specific building, use, or lease space it serves, preventing reviewers from verifying service assignments

WWP-22.16.deficiency: Meter-to-wastewater-tap correspondence not documented on plans or in the meter schedule, making one meter-one tap compliance unverifiable

WWP-22.17.deficiency: Submeter connections not documented with a schematic and service line sizes

WWP-22.18.deficiency: Multiple domestic water meters not identified as interconnected or independent on plans

WWP-22.19.deficiency: Separately metered interior spaces not identified on plans and door accesses not shown for those spaces

WWP-22.20.deficiency: Water meters on abandoned services not documented with size, type, and use (domestic or irrigation) on the plans — per UCM 2.8.4.B, the Engineer must call out size, type, and use for all meters to be abandoned, relocated, or re-purposed; water meter numbers are not required on plan sheets and are processed via the AW Taps Office form

WWP-22.21.deficiency: Fire demand meter proposed where domestic demand does not require a 3-inch or larger meter — per UCM 2.9.2.F.5, fire demand meters are allowed only when domestic demand necessitates a domestic meter of 3 inches or larger; if domestic demand requires a meter smaller than 3 inches, a dedicated fire line with double check detector backflow prevention assembly is required (or a single combined ≤2-inch meter where both fire and domestic demand can be served by a 2-inch or smaller meter)

WWP-22.22.deficiency: Domestic water service and irrigation/outdoor water service not provided as separate dedicated metered supplies for commercial or multifamily properties — irrigation served from the domestic meter causes double billing and wastewater surcharges; note that waiver is available per UCM 2.9.2.F.2.b under eight qualifying conditions (see Regulatory Overview)

WWP-22.23.deficiency: Domestic water line piping and fire line piping not shown as completely separate systems — tees or shared piping combining both services shown on utility plan — without documentation that a permitted exception applies under UCM 2.9.2.F.5 (small fire demand, combined ≤2-inch meter) or UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e (high-rise building with two-connection fire pump supply)

WWP-22.24.deficiency: Unmetered water lines serving building connections shown on plans — all water piping to buildings must originate from a metered potable water source

WWP-22.25.deficiency: Meter type not appropriate for intended use — turbine meters proposed for domestic service (turbine meters are permitted for irrigation only; domestic service requires positive displacement meters)

WWP-22.26.deficiency: Swimming pool or similar water feature on a commercial or multifamily property supplied from the domestic water meter — per UCM 2.9.2.F.2.a, pools are explicitly listed as outdoor uses requiring a separate AW meter for commercial and multifamily properties; waiver available per UCM 2.9.2.F.2.b

WWP-22.27.deficiency: Public water meters and their supply piping located on private property not shown within the boundaries of a recorded public utility easement on the utility plan

WWP-22.28.deficiency: Recorded public water easement documentation not provided for public water meters and supply piping on private property — easement documents must be reviewed and approved by AW Pipeline Engineering prior to county recordation, and recordation must precede AW construction plan approval per UCM 2.9.1.A.2

WWP-22.29.deficiency: Private water piping downstream of the meter not labeled as "Private" on plans, or size and material of private downstream piping not identified — downstream piping must be clearly distinguished to delineate AW maintenance jurisdiction

WWP-22.30.deficiency: Public vs. private side of the meter assembly not clearly delineated on the utility plan or an enlarged inset — the point at which AW-maintained infrastructure ends and customer-maintained infrastructure begins is not identified, preventing Austin Water Pipeline Engineering from verifying its review jurisdiction per UCM 2.5.1.A

WWP-22.31.deficiency: Meter locations, sizes, or service connections inconsistent between utility plan, existing conditions plan, and demo plan — e.g., meter shown as removed on demo plan but retained on utility plan

WWP-22.32.deficiency: Pipe diameter from the public main tap connection to the proposed meter not shown on the utility plan

WWP-22.33.deficiency: Water main connection point not clearly identified on the utility plan — proposed water service line shown connecting to an unknown or unlabeled line rather than an identified existing main

WWP-22.34.deficiency: Austin Water Standard Detail for water service and meter installation not included on the plans for 1-inch and smaller meters — per UCM 2.9.2.E.1, water services shall be in accordance with COA Standard Details

WWP-22.35.deficiency: Water meters (domestic, irrigation, fire service) not located in public ROW or in a dedicated easement immediately adjacent to the ROW — UCM 2.9.2.E.3 requires meter placement within the public ROW or immediately adjacent easement; "immediately adjacent" is not defined by a specific numeric distance and is evaluated case-by-case

WWP-22.36.deficiency: Reclaimed water meters not located within public ROW or in a dedicated easement immediately adjacent to the ROW — UCM 2.9.3.D.7 mirrors the potable meter location requirement

WWP-22.37.deficiency: Water meter vault straddles the property line — AW vaults outside the ROW must be placed entirely within a dedicated Exclusive Water Line Vault Easement with a minimum 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault per UCM 2.9.1.A.4; straddling the property line fails both the easement boundary and exclusive space requirements

WWP-22.38.deficiency: Meter with proposed private fire service connection not located within a dedicated public utility easement immediately adjacent to the ROW — per UCM 2.9.2.E.3, all meters must be within the public ROW or in an easement immediately adjacent to the ROW; no specific numeric distance defines "immediately adjacent"

WWP-22.39.deficiency: Water meters within state highway ROW not relocated to private property within a dedicated water line easement — AW cannot hold easement authority within TxDOT ROW; meters must be relocated per UCM 2.9.1.A.4 and UCM 2.9.1.B.1; a TxDOT encroachment/utility installation permit is required for any utilities remaining within or crossing TxDOT ROW

WWP-22.40.deficiency: Water meter boxes or appurtenances placed in sidewalks, paved areas, driveways, or load-bearing pavement — prohibited by UCM 2.9.2.E.3 for all meter types

WWP-22.41.deficiency: Water meter boxes placed within fenced areas — UCM 2.9.2.E.3 prohibits meters inside fences; fencing must be adjusted to maintain unobstructed vehicle access

WWP-22.42.deficiency: Water meters and vaults not accessible by service vehicle — per UCM 2.9.2.E.3, meters must be accessible by vehicle; reviewer should check for insufficient clearance from ROW for truck and crane access or absence of a pathway to the meter location

WWP-22.43.deficiency: Proposed water meters, meter boxes, or meter box lids not confirmed as conforming to Austin Water's automated metering infrastructure (AMI) technology and Standard Products List (SPL) — per UCM 2.9.2.F.6 and UCM 2.9.3.E, all new meters, meter boxes, and lids (potable and reclaimed) must conform to AW's AMI technology and the applicable SPL; site plan applicants are responsible for all AMI extension costs including DCU poles/structures, easements to the City, and electrical service to DCUs where solar power is not practical; all three components (meter, box, and lid) must be on the SPL

WWP-22.44.deficiency: Water or reclaimed water service line from the public main tap to the proposed meter shown or scaled at more than 55 feet in length on the utility plan — per UCM 2.9.2.E.8 (potable water and fire lines) and UCM 2.9.3.D.10 (reclaimed water), individual service lines shall not exceed 55 feet from the main to the meter; service lines that cross a divided road or highway (opposing lanes separated by a median, railroad tracks, or other obstruction per UCM 2.9.2.B.2) are prohibited regardless of length; a written UCM Waiver Request under UCM 2.9.6 is required if the 55-foot limit is exceeded

WWP-22.45.deficiency: Reclaimed water service to cooling towers or interior building uses not provided with a separate dedicated reclaimed water meter — per UCM 2.9.3.D.5, each cooling tower service or interior building use must have its own dedicated reclaimed water meter

WWP-23.1.deficiency: Water Service Fixture Unit (WSFU) calculation not provided for domestic meter sizing; demand not based on actual project characteristics; generic building-type lookup tables used instead of actual calculated demand; or building area/occupancy used in calculation is not accurate. For residential (1–2 family dwellings and townhomes), calculations must be based on Table 610.1 and provided at the WWSPV consultation. For commercial and other projects, a per-fixture WSFU count converted to GPM via UPC Chart A 103.1 is required — IPC tables and Hunter's Curve are not accepted.

WWP-23.2.deficiency: Domestic meter size not determined using the AWWA Water Meter Standards and Austin Water AWWA Meter Sizing Table; or calculated peak hour demand exceeds the safe operating capacity of the selected meter size. For residential (1–2 family dwellings and townhomes), meter must be sized per LDC § 25-12-153 Table 610.1.

WWP-23.3.deficiency: Domestic meter is significantly oversized beyond calculated peak hour demand; oversized meters produce inaccurate readings at low flow rates; documented justification not provided if upsizing is requested (e.g., for documented future expansion).

WWP-23.4.deficiency: When continuous operations at the safe maximum capacity flow rate are expected to exceed 2 hours per day, the AWWA recommended maximum continuous rate — not the safe maximum rate — has not been used for meter sizing.

WWP-23.5.deficiency: Domestic meter sizing calculations for a 3-inch or larger meter not prepared and sealed by a Texas-licensed Professional Engineer.

WWP-23.6.deficiency: When two or more domestic meters are proposed, separate peak hour demand calculations not provided for each meter individually.

WWP-23.7.deficiency: Redundant domestic meters proposed without justification based on actual demand; meter quantity not supported by plumbing code requirements; meters must be consolidated unless demand justification is provided.

WWP-23.8.deficiency: Water service line diameter not consistent with and not determined by demand calculations and meter size; service line and meter sizes do not match.

WWP-23.9.deficiency: Irrigation meter size determined from rated meter capacity rather than from calculated actual maximum irrigation system demand; demand must be calculated using the 8,100 gal/irrigated acre standard rate per Austin Water requirements. The irrigated area in acres must be explicitly labeled on the plans (1 acre = 43,560 SF if only square footage is shown).

WWP-23.10.deficiency: Irrigation demand calculation does not account for simultaneous zone operation, landscaped area, plant water requirements, precipitation rates, and evapotranspiration rates; demand value is unrealistic or inconsistent with the system design.

WWP-23.11.deficiency: When two or more irrigation meters are proposed, separate calculated demand values not provided for each meter individually; individual maximum demand values not documented separately.

WWP-23.12.deficiency: Irrigation meter service line size does not match the meter size (e.g., a 2-inch service is proposed with a meter smaller than 2 inches, or service saddle size is inconsistent with meter).

WWP-23.13.deficiency: Domestic meter smaller than 2 inches specified as turbine type; turbine meters are reserved for irrigation service only; domestic meters at this size must be compound or positive displacement type. Note: these type requirements derive from AWWA Water Meter Standards and the AW Standard Products List, which are not reproduced in Bureau — flag deviations from the meter type matrix for Austin Water verification.

WWP-23.14.deficiency: Domestic 2-inch meter specified as compound type; compound meters are not available at the 2-inch size; specify positive displacement or turbine per Austin Water AMI technology requirements. Note: specific approved models are on the AW Standard Products List.

WWP-23.15.deficiency: Domestic meter 3 inches or larger not specified as compound type; positive displacement meters are limited to a maximum size of 2 inches and must not be specified for larger domestic services.

WWP-23.16.deficiency: Domestic 4-inch meter specified as Turbine Class II type; compound type is specifically required for 4-inch domestic service; Turbine Class II does not provide accurate measurement across the full demand range at this size.

WWP-23.17.deficiency: Irrigation meter specified as positive displacement type rather than Turbine Class II; positive displacement type does not provide adequate performance and durability under sustained higher-flow irrigation operation.

WWP-23.18.deficiency: Non-standard or Austin Water–unapproved meter size specified (e.g., 2.5-inch, 1.6-inch); only standard approved meter sizes are permitted per the AW Standard Products List.

WWP-23.19.deficiency: Separate dedicated irrigation meter not provided for a commercial or multi-family property; all outdoor use, common area water, and permanently installed irrigation systems (including swimming pools, fountains, permanently installed irrigation, and quick-coupler hose bibbs) must be measured by a separate irrigation meter. "Commercial or multi-family" includes any project with MF-1 through MF-6, CS, GO, GR, LI, CH, CB, LR, CS-1, SF-6, or other commercial/multifamily zoning, and mixed-use buildings with residential and commercial components.

WWP-23.20.deficiency: Common area water uses not separately metered from individual unit domestic service.

WWP-23.21.deficiency: Irrigation meter not proposed for a commercial or multi-family property without a documented waiver from Austin Water. If an irrigation meter is omitted, the plans must identify which of the eight qualifying waiver conditions applies (UCM 2.9.2.F.2.b): (1) no landscaping; (2) no permanent automatic irrigation and multiple hose bibbs available; (3) commercial landscaping requirements do not apply; (4) ≥90% impervious cover; (5) new fire in-line installation; (6) AC condensate or alternative on-site water meets all outdoor demands; (7) change of use for interior remodeling; or (8) well water meets all outdoor demands. Plans that cite UCM 2.9.3.D as the waiver authority are incorrect — UCM 2.9.3.D governs reclaimed water service design (backflow prevention, purple pipe) and contains no potable water irrigation meter waiver provision.

WWP-23.22.deficiency: Combined fire-and-domestic meter proposed when domestic demand alone does not necessitate a meter 3 inches or larger (domestic demand below 152 GPM); combined meters are only permitted when domestic demand independently requires a 3-inch or larger meter. If domestic demand does not require a 3-inch+ meter, fire flow shall be via a separate dedicated fire line with a double check detector backflow prevention assembly per Austin Water Standard Detail. Exception: a single meter ≤2 inches is permissible for both fire and domestic when both demands are independently small enough to be served by a 2-inch or smaller meter (UCM 2.9.2.F.5 small fire demand exception).

WWP-23.23.deficiency: Combined fire-and-domestic meter not labeled as "Fire and Domestic" on plans; meter labeled as domestic only or without fire demand designation. Also verify that the meter size shown in plan view matches the size shown in profile view — inconsistency between views (e.g., profile shows 12-inch where plan view shows 8-inch) is a separate deficiency requiring correction.

WWP-23.24.deficiency: Combined fire-and-domestic meter (or fire service configuration) not sized to deliver required fire flow and domestic demand simultaneously; meter capacity in GPM not verified against the required fire flow demand.

WWP-23.25.deficiency: Combined total flow rate in GPM for all water service connections (domestic meter, irrigation meter, fire hydrants) not provided on plans; total demand not verified against proposed water main sizing for peak hour demand and emergency fire flow capacity.

WWP-23.26.deficiency: Development with 5 or more dwelling units not served by a single master meter with private submetering system; multiple individual Austin Water meters are not permitted for developments at this scale. Note: 2–4 unit properties require individual AW meters per unit; 5+ unit properties require a single master AW meter plus private sub-meters.

WWP-23.27.deficiency: Private submetering system for a 5+ dwelling unit development does not comply with PUCT and plumbing code requirements; each unit must have a single cold water stub-out supplying all fixtures, a privately owned meter per unit, a shut-off valve immediately ahead of each private meter, 4-inch clearance on each side, and the meter must be accessible. Exception: developments using alternate/reclaimed water for toilet flushing or with a centralized hot water system are not required to comply with the unit-level stub-out/meter layout requirement. Specifications or reference to applicable standards must be provided.

WWP-23.28.deficiency: Domestic meter 1-inch or smaller does not reference COA Standard Detail 520-AW-01B on plans; detail callout incomplete or missing required labeling (service clamp size, pipe diameter, material type).

WWP-23.29.deficiency: Domestic meter 1.5-inch to 2-inch does not reference COA Standard Detail 520-AW-01B; components shown (service tap, pipe materials, bends, valve type, meter orientation, spacing) do not match standard detail specifications.

WWP-23.30.deficiency: Domestic meter 3 inches or larger does not reference COA Standard Detail 520-AW-06; components do not match standard detail; bypass assembly configuration not included or not shown to comply with specified materials and layout.

WWP-23.31.deficiency: Irrigation meter installation does not reference the applicable COA Standard Detail (520S-19A, 520S-19C, or equivalent); complete callout not shown on plans.

WWP-23.32.deficiency: Meters 1-inch or smaller proposed to share a single service line without a double meter box; OR meters 1.5-inch or larger proposed to share a service line from the main (each meter 1.5-inch or larger requires its own separate dedicated service line). Specific requirements come from COA Standard Details referenced by UCM 2.9.2.E.1.

WWP-23.33.deficiency: Domestic and irrigation meters not located on the same side of the driveway; current placement would require service lines to cross under the driveway where they are vulnerable to traffic damage. Specific driveway-side placement requirements come from COA Standard Details referenced by UCM 2.9.2.E.1.

WWP-23.34.deficiency: Irrigation meter 1.5 inches or larger does not have its own dedicated tap on the water main; irrigation service is teed from a domestic service line or another service rather than tapped directly from the main.

WWP-23.35.deficiency: Irrigation meter not located immediately downstream of the tap to the main at the point where the irrigation line branches from the water service. Specific location requirements come from COA Standard Details referenced by UCM 2.9.2.E.1.

WWP-23.36.deficiency: Double meter installation uses a single service tee with two 1-inch meters; replace with a single 1.5-inch meter conforming to Standard Detail 520-AW-01B; dual 1-inch meters on a shared service tee are not permitted.

WWP-23.37.deficiency: Service tap size does not match service line size and meter requirements. Specific tap size requirements come from COA Standard Details referenced by UCM 2.9.2.E.1.

WWP-23.38.deficiency: Water meter box or appurtenance located outside of the public ROW or an easement immediately adjacent to the ROW; meter located inside a fence; meter not accessible by vehicle; or water meter box located in a sidewalk, paved area, driveway, or load-bearing pavement.

WWP-23.39.deficiency: Service taps to the water main have less than 3 feet of separation from one another.

WWP-23.40.deficiency: Domestic water service proposed to be supplied from a fire hydrant lead rather than from a direct tap to the water main.

WWP-23.41.deficiency: Individual water meter service line or fire line exceeds 55 feet in length from the water main to the water meter, or service line crosses a divided road or highway (a road where opposing lanes are currently or planned to be separated by a median, railroad tracks, or other vehicle obstruction); no UCM § 2.9.6 written Waiver Request is included in the submittal. If a service line exceeds 55 feet, a formal written waiver is required before approval — issuing a comment is appropriate when no waiver is present.

WWP-23.42.deficiency: Size of all proposed water meters not indicated on utility plans.

WWP-23.43.deficiency: Water meters not labeled on plans to clearly identify service type (domestic, irrigation, fire demand, reclaimed water, or combination); use designation missing or ambiguous.

WWP-23.44.deficiency: Complete meter specifications not documented for each meter: meter type, nominal diameter, GPM flow range as a complete operational range (minimum to maximum GPM — not a single value), and service units not all provided. The AW General Information Sheet (required by UCM 2.5.1.E.22) is the primary vehicle for this documentation.

WWP-23.45.deficiency: Meter size not specified by nominal diameter only; compound dimension designations (e.g., "2×2-inch" or "8×8-inch") used instead of nominal diameter designation.

WWP-23.46.deficiency: Service units for one or more meters not consistent with meter size, demand calculations, and applicable capital recovery fee schedule; irrigation meter service units not calculated per LDC § 25-9-331 to accurately reflect anticipated demand. Use the service units table in LDC § 25-9-331 to verify — service units are determined by both meter size and meter type (e.g., a 2-inch turbine meter is 10 service units while a 2-inch simple/compound meter is 8 service units).

WWP-23.47.deficiency: Irrigation meter location, size, and type not shown on water line plan.

WWP-23.48.deficiency: Irrigation meter velocity not verified at or below 5 fps; or proposed irrigation meter does not meet Austin Water AMI (automated metering infrastructure) technology requirements. All three components — meter, meter box, and meter box lid — must be on the AW Standard Products List. Site plan applicants are responsible for AMI extension costs including DCU infrastructure and easement.

WWP-23.49.deficiency: Building Water Meter Size Table not included per AW General Notes Sheet template for a multi-building project; or table is included but not deleted for a single-building project where it is not applicable. This table is part of the AW General Information and Construction Notes Sheet required by UCM 2.5.1.E.22 — it is not governed by BCM 15.4.A.1 (which addresses tap plan review timelines).

WWP-23.50.deficiency: Number of required irrigation meters not documented in the Irrigation Meter(s) Requirement field on the AW General Notes Sheet.

WWP-23.51.deficiency: Multiple irrigation meters proposed without individual demand values documented separately for each meter in the demand data table; each meter must have its own maximum demand value, size, GPM range, and service address.

WWP-23.52.deficiency: Existing water meter on-site not identified as domestic or irrigation type; plans do not clarify whether the existing meter can be reused for the proposed development or must be replaced/supplemented.

WWP-24.1.deficiency: Domestic water demand calculations do not use the UCM 2.9.2.A.1 prescribed rates: 200 gpd/person (average day), 530 gpd/person (peak day), and 900 gpd/person (peak hour). Rates from other plumbing codes or standards must not be substituted.

WWP-24.2.deficiency: Emergency demand is not correctly computed in the FIRE, DOMESTIC AND IRRIGATION DEMAND DATA table. UCM 2.9.2.A.3.a defines emergency demand as fire flow plus peak day demands; the AW General Information Sheet format (required by UCM 2.5.1.E.22) presents this as three separately visible components — fire, peak day domestic, and irrigation — all of which must be summed into the emergency demand total when applicable. Plans where the emergency demand row equals only fire flow plus domestic GPM, without a corresponding irrigation component when irrigation is proposed on the site, understate emergency demand.

WWP-24.3.deficiency: WSFU calculations are not provided in accordance with the applicable Uniform Plumbing Code (2015, 2021, or 2024 as applicable to the project), as adopted by reference per LDC § 25-12-151(A).

WWP-24.4.deficiency: WSFU calculations are not broken down by individual fixture type, showing quantity and fixture unit value assigned to each type (e.g., water closets, lavatories, sinks, bathtubs, hose bibbs).

WWP-24.5.deficiency: Public and private toilet fixtures are not distinguished in WSFU calculations. Under UPC Table 702.1 (adopted by LDC § 25-12-151(A)), public fixtures — those in common or commercial restrooms accessible to the general public — carry different WSFU values than private fixtures in individual dwelling units; failing to distinguish them produces an incorrect fixture unit total.

WWP-24.6.deficiency: WSFU calculations and all fixture counts are not shown on the plans; supporting documentation must be included in the submittal.

WWP-24.7.deficiency: Incomplete WSFU notations (e.g., ">60 WSFU") are used instead of the actual full calculated fixture unit value derived from a complete fixture schedule. Approximate or bounded values cannot be verified against UPC Chart A 103.1 and cannot support meter sizing.

WWP-24.8.deficiency: WSFU is incorrectly labeled as "LUEs," "DFU," "Fixture Counts," or another non-standard designation; all water supply fixture unit values must be labeled "WSFU." Mislabeling creates definitional errors that undermine downstream calculations and cross-document consistency checks.

WWP-24.9.deficiency: Water heater sizing calculation has not been provided in accordance with the applicable Uniform Plumbing Code, as adopted by reference per LDC § 25-12-151(A).

WWP-24.10.deficiency: When a sprinkler system is present, its inclusion or exclusion from WSFU or DFU calculations is not documented and the fixture unit value assigned (if included) is not explained.

WWP-24.11.deficiency: WSFU are not converted to GPM demand using UPC Chart A 103.1 (the only acceptable conversion method, adopted by reference via LDC § 25-12-151(A)). Use of Hunter's Curve, IPC tables, or other non-UPC conversion tools is non-compliant. The regulatory authority chain is: UCM 2.9.2.F.4.b (pipe and meter size per plumbing code) → LDC § 25-12-151(A) (adopts UPC including Appendix A / Chart A 103.1). Look for: demand table that cites "Hunter's Curve," references IPC, or shows a GPM value that does not match the Chart A 103.1 output for the stated WSFU total.

WWP-24.12.deficiency: The fixture type — either Flush Tanks or Flushometers — is not circled or clearly selected in the WSFU row of the FIRE, DOMESTIC AND IRRIGATION DEMAND DATA table, as required by the AW General Information Sheet form per UCM 2.5.1.E.22.

WWP-24.13.deficiency: The selected fixture type (Flush Tanks or Flushometers) does not match the actual plumbing fixtures specified in the building's plumbing design plans.

WWP-24.14.deficiency: The fixture type selection (Flush Tanks or Flushometers) is not consistently applied across WSFU calculations, peak demand determinations, service line sizing, and meter sizing; the selection must propagate through all downstream calculations because flush tank and flushometer fixtures carry different UPC Table 702.1 values.

WWP-24.15.deficiency: DFU calculations are not provided in accordance with the applicable Uniform Plumbing Code (adopted by reference per LDC § 25-12-151(A)) and are not broken down by individual fixture type showing quantity and unit value for each type.

WWP-24.16.deficiency: DFU is not provided separately for each building, each wastewater connection point, and each section of private wastewater piping served by the proposed system.

WWP-24.17.deficiency: DFU is not provided for each proposed lift station.

WWP-24.18.deficiency: DFU tables do not identify which building or system element each table serves; table headers and row labels must specify the associated building, use type, or facility.

WWP-24.19.deficiency: DFU table title does not clearly indicate "Private Drainage Fixture Units" to distinguish private building drain fixtures from public sewer loading calculations, or DFU tables use non-DFU units (e.g., WSFU or GPM). Under the adopted 2024 UPC (LDC § 25-12-151(A)), Table 702.1 assigns different DFU values to public versus private fixtures; tables covering only private building drain fixtures must be explicitly labeled "Private" to prevent misapplication of incorrect fixture unit values. Note: UCM 2.9.4.G.5, which was previously cited for this item, governs the 9-foot physical separation between water and wastewater service lines — it has no bearing on DFU table labeling.

WWP-24.20.deficiency: For projects with multiple wastewater service connections to the public main, call-outs showing DFU amounts and flow percentages at each connection point are not provided on the wastewater collection plan.

WWP-24.21.deficiency: DFU is not provided for existing buildings that are connected to new or modified wastewater infrastructure.

WWP-24.22.deficiency: When WSFU and DFU values show an unusual or significant disparity (considering that some difference is expected because fixture types have different supply and drainage unit values), detailed calculations and explanation are not provided to justify the difference.

WWP-24.23.deficiency: Irrigation demand is not calculated at 8,100 gallons per irrigated acre for maximum day flow per UCM 2.9.3.A.2.c.i. This rate is the fixed AW-prescribed standard for both reclaimed water irrigation (explicitly required by UCM 2.9.3.A.2.c.i) and potable water irrigation (applied as an AW administrative standard).

WWP-24.24.deficiency: Irrigation demand is not expressed in GPM (and FPS) as required by the AW General Information Sheet form format.

WWP-24.25.deficiency: Irrigation demand is shown as a standalone "MAXIMUM IRRIGATION DEMAND" row outside the emergency demand section of the FIRE, DOMESTIC AND IRRIGATION DEMAND DATA table, preventing verification that all required components — fire, domestic, and irrigation — are properly summed into the emergency demand total. The AW General Information Sheet format (required by UCM 2.5.1.E.22) requires irrigation demand to appear as a component within the emergency demand calculation, not as a separate unrelated line item.

WWP-24.26.deficiency: Wastewater flow calculations for residential portions of the project do not use the UCM 2.9.4.A.1 mandatory rate of 245 gallons per day per residential unit plus applicable inflow/infiltration allowances. The 245 gpd rate is required for all residential dwelling units and no project-specific lower estimate may substitute it.

WWP-24.27.deficiency: Peak dry weather flow (PDWF) is not calculated using the UCM 2.9.4.A.4 formula: Qpd = [(18+(0.0206×F)^0.5)/(4+(0.0206×F)^0.5)]×F, where F = (70 gal./person/day × population) / 1440 (F must be in gpm, not gpd — the division by 1440 converts to gallons per minute).

WWP-24.28.deficiency: Peak wet weather flow (PWWF) is not calculated as PDWF plus inflow/infiltration (I/I) at 750 gallons per day per acre served per UCM 2.9.4.A.3 and 2.9.4.A.5. Projects in the Edwards Aquifer Zone must use TCEQ I/I requirements instead.

WWP-24.29.deficiency: Wastewater profile sheets do not show PDWF and PWWF with associated pipe velocities for each proposed gravity pipe segment, as required by UCM 2.5.3.B.7. Both peak dry weather flow and peak wet weather flow values, along with the velocity in each pipe section, must appear on the profile sheets.

WWP-24.30.deficiency: Living Unit Equivalent (LUE) calculations are not provided for wastewater capacity determination per UCM 2.9.4.A.1. LUE applies to residential projects: 1 LUE = 1 residential dwelling unit = 245 gpd average wastewater flow. Commercial, office, industrial, and institutional projects do not use LUE methodology and should not show LUE values.

WWP-24.31.deficiency: LUE values appear in the water demand section of the FIRE, DOMESTIC AND IRRIGATION DEMAND DATA table. LUE is a wastewater capacity metric (1 LUE = 1 residential unit = 245 gpd) and must appear only in the wastewater/LUE section of the table — not as a line item in domestic water demand calculations.

WWP-24.32.deficiency: Each building is not numbered on the utility plan, or LUE counts are not shown on each building label on the utility plan, as required by UCM 2.9.4.A.1.

WWP-26.63.deficiency: Meter information not reviewed and approved by AWPE before final approval is granted.

WWP-26.64.deficiency: Cooling tower presence (or confirmed absence) not documented in project summary for AW review purposes.

WWP-27.1.deficiency: Dedicated utility easement not provided for water, wastewater, or reclaimed water mains located outside public ROW.

WWP-27.2.deficiency: Wastewater service connections or cleanouts crossing lot lines outside public ROW are not within a dedicated water/wastewater easement of minimum 5-foot × 5-foot dimensions.

WWP-27.3.deficiency: Fire service lines or fire hydrant assemblies extending outside public ROW are not within a dedicated utility easement.

WWP-27.4.deficiency: Backflow preventer installations outside public ROW are not within a dedicated water line easement.

WWP-27.5.deficiency: Wastewater force mains or lift stations outside public ROW are not within a dedicated Water and Wastewater easement.

WWP-27.6.deficiency: Austin Water vault(s) outside ROW are not designated as "Exclusive Water Line Vault Easement," or an incorrect name is applied (e.g., "Public Utility Easement," "Water Lines Vault Easement," "Exclusive Water Vault," "Water Meter Vault Easement," or any other variant).

WWP-27.7.deficiency: Reclaimed water vault outside ROW is not designated as a separate "Exclusive Reclaimed Water Line Vault Easement" — domestic water and reclaimed water cannot share the same vault easement.

WWP-27.8.deficiency: Water infrastructure outside ROW without a vault structure is incorrectly designated with a vault easement rather than the proper "Water Lines Easement" designation for pipe-only installations.

WWP-27.9.deficiency: Exclusive vault easement does not provide a minimum 5-foot exclusive space around and under the vault structure, or elements other than an associated irrigation service (e.g., other utilities, structures, or appurtenances) are placed within this 5-foot exclusive space.

WWP-27.10.deficiency: Vault easement dimensions are not shown on profile views, or profile views do not demonstrate the required 5-foot vertical clearance above and below the vault structure.

WWP-27.11.deficiency: Utility easement width is less than 15 feet, or less than twice the infrastructure depth from finished grade to flowline (whichever is greater), or utility infrastructure is not centered within the easement boundaries.

WWP-27.12.deficiency: Fill is proposed over an existing utility easement without a corresponding adjustment to easement width to meet the minimum width requirements based on the new cover depth (15 ft or twice the new finished grade to flowline depth, whichever is greater).

WWP-27.13.deficiency: Water meter is not placed within the public ROW or in an easement immediately adjacent to the ROW; or the water meter easement does not meet minimum required dimensions per AW Standard Details; or meter box or appurtenances are placed in a sidewalk, paved area, driveway, or load-bearing pavement.

WWP-27.14.deficiency: Permanent structures (buildings, retaining walls, baffles, berms, or storage areas) are placed within utility easement boundaries or directly over water or wastewater infrastructure, obstructing AW maintenance access.

WWP-27.15.deficiency: Benches, site furnishings, or landscaping features are placed over water or wastewater lines or within utility easement areas, restricting AW maintenance access.

WWP-27.16.deficiency: Trees are planted within wastewater easement boundaries.

WWP-27.17.deficiency: Pressure reducing valves (domestic or irrigation PRVs) installed outside the building footprint are located within a public utility easement rather than on private property outside the easement.

WWP-27.18.deficiency: Double Check Detector Assembly (DCDA) vault is located within a public utility easement rather than on private property outside the easement. A DCDA is a backflow prevention assembly installed on unmetered private fire service lines; it typically appears in fire line connection details or service diagrams on utility plan sheets.

WWP-27.19.deficiency: Private fire lines (privately owned fire service lines from the AW main to the building's fire suppression system) are routed within a public utility easement rather than on private property outside the easement.

WWP-27.20.deficiency: Private plumbing runs in parallel within and along a public utility easement, or crosses the easement at more than 45° from perpendicular (i.e., at less than 45° from parallel) rather than perpendicularly or within 45° of perpendicular. Any parallel routing within the easement boundaries is prohibited — there is no de minimis exception for short parallel segments.

WWP-27.21.deficiency: Service cleanouts are placed within an electric, gas, or other non-water/wastewater utility easement; or a cleanout adjacent to a public utility easement is not positioned at the easement edge as required for lots without a dedicated water/wastewater easement.

WWP-27.22.deficiency: All-weather vehicle access road (minimum 12 feet wide) within a dedicated access easement (minimum 20 feet wide) is not provided for wastewater infrastructure and Austin Water utility features (manholes, valves, air release assemblies) located outside public ROW and not otherwise accessible from an existing all-weather road.

WWP-27.23.deficiency: Wastewater easement proposed to serve in lieu of a separate all-weather access easement is less than the minimum 20-foot width required to accommodate the access road and comply with UCM 2.9.4.D.12.

WWP-27.24.deficiency: All-weather access road does not meet UCM 2.9.4.D.12 design criteria: maximum 15% longitudinal slope, 5% transverse slope, or 12% maximum vertical grade break is exceeded; inside turning radius is less than 28.3 feet or outside turning radius is less than 42 feet; horizontal or vertical clearance from vegetation or objects is less than 14 feet; or equipment turnaround is not provided where the access road extends more than 200 feet from a paved public roadway.

WWP-27.25.deficiency: Existing utility easement access is not clear and unobstructed — fences, structures, or improvements block access to public cleanouts or other Austin Water utility features and have not been relocated to restore access.

WWP-27.26.deficiency: All existing and proposed easements (drainage, electric, gas, water/wastewater/reclaimed, public utility lines and manholes, private utility lines, re-irrigation, access, conservation, and others) are not shown on all applicable plan sheets (utility plan, site plan, drainage sheet, grading plan, ESC sheet, paving plan).

WWP-27.27.deficiency: Easements on adjacent or neighboring properties that contain utilities or infrastructure relevant to the project are not shown with recording information on applicable plan sheets.

WWP-27.28.deficiency: Easements depicted on plans are inconsistent with or do not match the recorded plat documents; discrepancies between plat and plan representations are not resolved.

WWP-27.29.deficiency: Recorded easement document numbers (volume/page or Travis County Document Number/clerk's file number) are missing from plan sheets where each recorded easement is depicted.

WWP-27.30.deficiency: Easement document numbers shown on plans are invalid or do not match official Travis County Clerk records; numbers are transposed, estimated, or copied from stale plan versions.

WWP-27.31.deficiency: Easement recording information is not listed in the cover sheet notes or in the LUE Tracking Table (or AW Infrastructure Information Table) for all recorded easements and temporary working spaces.

WWP-27.32.deficiency: Easement labels do not spell out the full legal title from the recorded document; abbreviations such as "P.U.E.," "W.E.," "S.E.," or "D.E." are used instead of full designations such as "Public Utility Easement," "Water Lines Easement," "Sewer Easement," or "Drainage Easement."

WWP-27.33.deficiency: Generic easement labels (e.g., "15' WATER EASEMENT," "10' WATER EASEMENT") are used instead of the proper official UCM designation (e.g., "Water Lines Easement," "Exclusive Water Line Vault Easement") for AW utility easements.

WWP-27.34.deficiency: Easements are not identified as public or private on applicable plan sheets, or labels are not applied consistently across all applicable plan sheets (site plan, utility plan, landscape plan, drainage sheet).

WWP-27.35.deficiency: Metes and bounds (bearings and distances) are not provided for all easement boundaries in plan view, or easement boundary lines do not extend to and intersect the ROW boundary to establish the complete legal extent required for recordation.

WWP-27.36.deficiency: Easement boundary dimensions are not shown on profile views and cross-sections, or easement limits and horizontal extents (station range) are not annotated on profile views.

WWP-27.37.deficiency: Easement dimensions shown on plans do not match the dimensions documented in the recorded easement documents or City of Austin records; discrepancies not corrected.

WWP-27.38.deficiency: Proposed (unrecorded) easements are not labeled as "PROPOSED," or do not include a placeholder line for the document number to be filled in after recordation.

WWP-27.39.deficiency: Easement status (existing vs. proposed) is not clearly distinguished throughout the plan set; proposed easements appear on demolition or existing conditions sheets where they should not.

WWP-27.40.deficiency: Water or wastewater easements are proposed to be dedicated "BY PLAT" rather than by separate recorded instrument, or the legal dedication method and instrument type are not specified prior to construction plan approval.

WWP-27.41.deficiency: Vacated easements are not shown on demolition plans with recording information and notation that they are vacated; or record document numbers are not updated after vacation.

WWP-27.42.deficiency: Easement documents and metes and bounds legal descriptions have not been submitted to Austin Water Pipeline Engineering (AWPE) for review and approval prior to recordation in county real property records.

WWP-27.43.deficiency: Easements have not been recorded in county real property records prior to construction plan approval; project remains pending in AMANDA pending AW approval and county recordation.

WWP-27.44.deficiency: The "GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS TO SUBMIT AW EASEMENT DOCUMENTS" note block is missing from the plan sheet.

WWP-27.45.deficiency: Cover sheet does not include a note stating that no public utility construction may begin until the water/wastewater easement is approved by Austin Water, recorded with the county, and a copy provided to Austin Water.

WWP-27.46.deficiency: Plan set does not include a note establishing that vaults, backflow devices, and privately owned water lines are private, and that the developer grants ingress and egress to Austin Water for meter reading and inspection.

WWP-27.48.deficiency: Easement cover sheet is missing required elements: date, case number, case name, contact information (owner/agent/attorney/engineer), document type, purpose, survey notes, exhibits, and lien-holder consent.

WWP-28.1.deficiency: Water SER not obtained when the existing water main cannot supply the required fire flow for the proposed use without exceeding the maximum velocity of 10 fps or dropping below the minimum residual pressure of 20 psi at peak day plus fire flow conditions, rendering existing service unsuitable or insufficient

WWP-28.2.deficiency: Written verification from Austin Water not provided confirming the §25-9-31 exception applies — i.e., that the Director has determined the existing system provides suitable and sufficient service per the UCM and the property boundary is within 100 feet of an accessible water main — when no water SER has been submitted

WWP-28.3.deficiency: Water SER not obtained when the proposed connection is to a water main 24 inches in diameter or larger (water transmission main). Direct retail service connections to transmission mains are not allowed without a Director exception. Note: Austin Water may designate a main smaller than 24 inches as a transmission main based on system function; if the connection point main is labeled less than 24 inches but may function as a transmission main, flag for Austin Water verification

WWP-28.4.deficiency: Water SER not obtained when the site is located within an AW-designated water pressure concern area, where existing water infrastructure cannot meet UCM pressure or velocity standards, rendering it unsuitable or insufficient

WWP-28.5.deficiency: Water SER not obtained when water meters are proposed in a location other than the public ROW or an easement immediately adjacent to the ROW — such meter placement renders existing service unsuitable or insufficient and constitutes meters on private lines

WWP-28.6.deficiency: Water and/or wastewater SER not obtained when the lot's only available utility frontage is IH-35. IH-35's right-of-way typically contains large-diameter water transmission mains (≥24 inches) that prohibit direct retail connections, triggering the large-diameter main or distance SER requirement. This is an Austin Water operational practice — the underlying code trigger is the large-diameter main or >100-foot distance criterion, not IH-35 frontage as an independent provision

WWP-28.7.deficiency: Water and/or wastewater SER not obtained when a new connection to a water or wastewater main within an alley is proposed. Alley connections typically trigger the large-diameter main or >100-foot distance SER requirements under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(1)–(2). This is an Austin Water operational practice

WWP-28.8.deficiency: SER revision not submitted when fire demand shown on current site plans is higher than the demand in the previously approved SER, requiring an amended SER application for changed anticipated water demands

WWP-28.9.deficiency: Wastewater SER not obtained when the site is located within an AW-designated wastewater capacity concern area, where existing wastewater infrastructure has insufficient capacity to serve the proposed development

WWP-28.10.deficiency: Wastewater SER not obtained when private wastewater piping is proposed to cross lot lines — a configuration that renders existing service unsuitable or insufficient, as private piping extending through another lot without a proper easement cannot constitute suitable and sufficient service

WWP-28.11.deficiency: Wastewater SER not obtained when the proposed connection is to a wastewater main larger than 15 inches in diameter. Service connections to mains >15 inches are prohibited (UCM 2.9.4.G.3); a main ≥18 inches constitutes a wastewater interceptor to which direct retail connections are not allowed without a Director exception (LDC § 25-9-32(14)). Because standard gravity sewer sizes jump from 15" directly to 18" (UCM 2.9.4.B.6), these thresholds are operationally equivalent — any main exceeding 15" will be an 18"+ interceptor

WWP-28.12.deficiency: Wastewater SER not obtained when a public wastewater main extension greater than 100 feet in length is proposed, extending the service beyond the 100-foot proximity exception

WWP-28.13.deficiency: Wastewater SER not obtained when a public wastewater force main extension is proposed

WWP-28.14.deficiency: Reclaimed water SER not obtained when reclaimed water service is proposed

WWP-28.15.deficiency: SER has not been fully approved before plan review proceeds — a DRAFT SER, pending SER, or absent SER does not satisfy the requirement. The SER must bear all required signatures, a dated approval, and no DRAFT watermark

WWP-28.16.deficiency: Previously approved SER has expired and has not been renewed before plan approval. For SERs approved on or after April 1, 2013, the SER expires on the latest of: 180 days after approval, the date a pending development application expires, or the date an approved development application expires. Exception: a recorded plat prevents expiration for the platted portion

WWP-28.17.deficiency: Wastewater SER does not include required Austin Fire Department (AFD) and Industrial Waste departmental sign-offs before plan review proceeds. Austin Water's internal processing requires wastewater SERs to bear AFD and Industrial Waste sign-off blocks with signatures in addition to Austin Water's approval. This is an Austin Water operational requirement; the absence of these sign-offs is visible as blank or unsigned approval blocks on the SER document

WWP-28.18.deficiency: SER number listed in the plan set has not been verified to correspond to this project's address and scope — the SER may belong to a different project or address

WWP-28.19.deficiency: SER application not accompanied by an annexation request when the property is outside Austin Water's Certificate of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) area. Austin Water's CCN area is coterminous with the adopted Water and Wastewater Impact Fee Service Area boundary

WWP-28.20.deficiency: When permitting is contingent on the status of offsite wastewater improvements not yet built or approved, status has not been confirmed with Austin Water

WWP-28.21.deficiency: Blank water SER block present on plan sheet when a water SER is not applicable to this project

WWP-28.22.deficiency: Blank wastewater SER block present on plan sheet when a wastewater SER is not applicable to this project

WWP-28.23.deficiency: When no water or wastewater SER is required for the project, plan sheet does not include the required note: "No Water or Wastewater Service Extension Requests (SERs) are required for this project"

WWP-28.24.deficiency: Placeholder emails, temporary text, or draft SER correspondence present on plan sheets in the final submitted plan set

WWP-28.25.deficiency: DRAFT watermark not removed from SER documentation included in the final plan set

WWP-28.26.deficiency: Submitted SER document is not legible — blurry, faded, or otherwise unreadable, preventing verification of capacity allocations and required information. An illegible document does not constitute provision of required information

WWP-28.27.deficiency: Required fields in the SER block are not fully completed — SER number, project name, Austin Water project number, water service number, and/or wastewater service number are missing or left blank

WWP-28.28.deficiency: Approved SER document not included on or with the AW General Information and Construction Notes Sheet as required

WWP-28.29.deficiency: AWU Information Sheet not updated to include current fire flow test data and SER documentation

WWP-28.30.deficiency: Plans do not include the Reclaimed Water and Onsite Water Reuse System Meter Demand Sheet required for projects with reclaimed water service or onsite water reuse systems, per UCM 2.5.1.E.22 as updated by Rule R161-24.02 (effective 5-8-2024)

WWP-28.31.deficiency: SER application submitted as a notation on the construction plans rather than through the formal SER application process directed to the Director. A service extension application must be submitted separately to the Director — plan-sheet notations do not substitute for a formal application

WWP-28.32.deficiency: Plan and profile details for all water SER-required improvements not included in the plan set (pipe sizes, alignments, valve locations, hydrant locations)

WWP-28.33.deficiency: Plan and profile details for all wastewater SER-required improvements not included in the plan set (gravity main extensions, alignment, sizing, connection points)

WWP-28.34.deficiency: Offsite utility improvements required by the approved SER not incorporated into the plan set

WWP-28.35.deficiency: Wastewater connection point shown on plans does not match the location specified in the approved SER

WWP-28.36.deficiency: Wastewater main alignment does not comply with the distance and location requirements specified in the approved SER

WWP-28.37.deficiency: Easement extension required by the approved WW SER not designed and shown in the plan set. Easements must be a minimum of 15 feet wide or twice the depth from finished grade to infrastructure flowline, whichever is greater, with infrastructure centered in the easement

WWP-28.38.deficiency: Wastewater gravity main linear footage shown on plans does not match the footage specified in the approved WW SER

WWP-28.39.deficiency: Wastewater design flow rates and/or phase information shown in the plans do not match the approved SER

WWP-28.40.deficiency: LUE count shown in the plans exceeds the LUE count approved in the associated SER. 1 LUE = 1 residential dwelling unit = 245 gpd; LUE count must match proposed dwelling unit count

WWP-28.41.deficiency: SER revision or amendment not submitted when the proposed LUE count exceeds the SER-approved count, fire demand has increased, or project scope has expanded since the original SER determination — all of which constitute changes to anticipated water or wastewater demands requiring an amended SER application

WWP-28.42.deficiency: Lot configuration has changed since the SER was approved (e.g., replat, lot split, or combination of lots) but no amended SER application has been filed. WWP-28.43.deficiency: Connection point(s) shown in the plans are not authorized by the approved SER

WWP-28.45.deficiency: When multiple SERs apply to the project, plans do not clearly identify which SER scope is being constructed as part of this project and which improvements are deferred or constructed under a separate permit

WWP-28.46.deficiency: SER documentation does not include sufficient information to verify the service extension's location, size, and capacity. This requirement is typically satisfied by SER maps showing service area boundaries, existing infrastructure locations, proposed extension routes, and connection points — but a detailed written description also satisfies the requirement; the code requires a "general description," not specifically maps

WWP-28.47.deficiency: Reclaimed water service line routing and meter location not shown on plans when reclaimed water service is included in the approved SER scope

WWP-28.48.deficiency: Water or wastewater main lines to be constructed by others are not identified with all three required elements: project name, Austin Water project number, and SER number. The label "by others" or "proposed by others" alone without all three identifiers is non-compliant

WWP-28.50.deficiency: Plans do not clarify which routing option from the approved SER is being constructed by this project, or fail to identify the AW project number and SER number if the SER routing was previously completed by another project

WWP-28.53.deficiency: Cover sheet does not include a note identifying the separate project that designed and permitted the off-site infrastructure required as a condition of the approved SER

WWP-28.55.deficiency: When wastewater service is contingent on a future City capital improvement project (e.g., a future WWTP upgrade), the SER map does not include a note indicating the Phase 2 wastewater service dependency

WWP-29.12.deficiency: Proposed connection to existing water main uses a tapping sleeve for a ≥4-inch connection without documented Austin Water case-by-case approval; "size-on-size" tap configuration proposed (not permitted); reconnection to an existing tapping sleeve proposed (expressly prohibited); PE pipe branch connection does not use an electrofusion coupler per SPL WW-706C

WWP-29.19.deficiency: Tap permit not obtained from Austin Water for new public service connections to the public main; separate complete plan set not submitted to Austin Water permitting office after site plan approval

WWP-29.20.deficiency: Proof of registration with the Public Utility Commission of Texas not provided for proposed water or sewer submetering or allocation services

WWP-29.21.deficiency: Subdivision within 100 feet of an existing public water system has not demonstrated required connection to the public water system; water system plans not approved by the director and installation not confirmed before lot occupation

WWP-29.22.deficiency: Subdivision within 100 feet of an existing public wastewater system within the zoning jurisdiction has not demonstrated required connection to the public wastewater system; wastewater lines not shown as installed before lot occupation

WWP-29.24.deficiency: When converting from on-site septic to municipal wastewater service, existing septic tank abandonment requirements, fees, and inspections not coordinated with Austin Water; separate OSSF abandonment application and fee required under City Code Chapter 15-5; existing OSSF components (septic tank, drainfield) not addressed on demolition/existing conditions plan sheets

WWP-29.26.deficiency: Sanitary sewer flow calculations not provided; residential flow not calculated at 245 gallons per day per dwelling unit (1 LUE = 245 gpd); commercial or industrial flows calculated using the 245 gpd/LUE method instead of person-based or case-by-case methods; I/I not included at 750 gal/day/acre served; or PDWF and PWWF not tabulated per UCM 2.9.4.A

WWP-29.27.deficiency: Capacity analysis not provided demonstrating existing water and wastewater infrastructure meets project demands; pipe capacity thresholds not verified (PDWF ≤ 65% of full-flow capacity for ≤15-inch mains; PWWF ≤ 85% for ≤15-inch mains or ≤ 80% for ≥18-inch mains); minimum design velocity at PDWF not demonstrated (minimum 2 fps, or written substantiation and minimum 1% grade if 2 fps cannot be achieved)

WWP-29.28.deficiency: Proposed Load Equivalent Units (LUEs) exceed available wastewater service capacity for the service area without demonstrated resolution (scope reduction, phased infrastructure, or written capacity allocation approval from Austin Water); wastewater capacity concern area designation present in facts.md or Austin Water correspondence without corresponding WARF (Wastewater Availability Request Form) confirmation of available capacity

WWP-32.23.deficiency: 1.5"–2" water meter installation design must comply with Standard Detail 520-AW-04, including service line sizing, materials, valve placement, and installation configuration

WWP-32.27.deficiency: Wastewater service line notes must not reference plumbing code for pipe materials; wastewater services must reference City of Austin Standard Details, which supersede plumbing code material references

WWP-32.28.deficiency: Wastewater service line abandonments must comply with COA Standard Details and must not include valves

WWP-32.29.deficiency: Fire hydrant assemblies must be designed and installed in accordance with the current Standard Detail 511-AW-02 (adopted 11/08/2023), including configurations for PRV installations and deep water mains

WWP-32.30.deficiency: PRV installations must comply with COA Standard Details per UCM 2.9.2.G, including location on private property outside of public utility easements, vault construction, drainage requirements, and spacing

WWP-32.31.deficiency: Connections of new mains (4 inches and larger) to existing mains must be made by cutting in a tee per UCM 2.9.2.B.11; tee connections to existing cast iron water mains must comply with Standard Details 520S-19A and 520S-19C (including fitting type, valve placement, joint restraint, and fire hydrant lead requirements); note that open-cut utility crossings under cast-iron mains with lead caulk joints are not permitted per UCM 2.9.2.B.18 and require main removal and replacement, or a supporting design detail when trench width is 3 feet or less

WWP-32.32.deficiency: Tracer wire notes must comply with COA Standard Details per UCM 2.9.2.B.3 and SSM Item No. 510.2(8)(j); inductive tracer detection tape must be placed above the centerline of all non-metallic pipe, color-coded per APWA Uniform Color Code, and from a manufacturer listed on SPL WW-597; do not use non-COA specifications

WWP-32.33.deficiency: Wastewater main placement at proposed connection stations must comply with standard utility assignments per the COA Standard Details Manual; alternative utility assignments require written approval from AW Utility Development Services (Pipeline Engineering)

WWP-32.34.deficiency: All Austin Water construction details must be consolidated on dedicated AW detail sheets; AW details must not be intermixed with details from drainage, transportation, parking, erosion control, or other departments

WWP-32.35.deficiency: Private infrastructure details (e.g., grinder pumps, private service connections, private wastewater systems, Dayton Grinder Pump specifications) must be on separate private detail sheets, not interspersed with public utility standard details

WWP-32.36.deficiency: Storm drainage manhole details must not appear on Austin Water utility detail sheets; they must be segregated to appropriate drainage sheets

WWP-32.37.deficiency: Fire hydrant assembly details must be located on a Water Distribution Details sheet, not on wastewater detail sheets

WWP-32.38.deficiency: Portrait-oriented Austin Water standard details must be limited to a maximum of 8 detail images per sheet; portrait-oriented details must be sized to utilize the entire sheet

WWP-32.39.deficiency: Landscape-oriented Austin Water standard details must be provided on dedicated full-size sheets

WWP-32.40.deficiency: All Austin Water standard details must be legible
