WWP-32.42.deficiency: Non-applicable standard details that do not correspond to proposed infrastructure, meter sizes, or site conditions must be removed from the plan set (e.g., 520-AW-01B if no 1" meters proposed; 520S-19B if no master meter is listed on General Notes)

WWP-32.43.deficiency: If Standard Detail 520S-19A or 520S-19B (fire line with master meter) is included in the plan set, the fire line must be listed on the Project Information Table on the Austin Water General Notes Sheet; if no master meter is proposed, replace 520S-19B with 520S-19C

WWP-32.44.deficiency: Clean-out design must comply with UCM 2.9.4.G.6; cleanouts are not allowed in sidewalks, paved areas, load bearing pavement, or driveways; non-compliant custom cleanout-in-paved-areas details must be removed from plan sets

WWP-32.45.deficiency: New water meters, meter boxes, and meter box lids must conform to AW's automated metering infrastructure (AMI) technology and the applicable Standard Products List; the same requirement applies to reclaimed water meters and meter boxes

WWP-32.46.deficiency: Fire lines must be constructed of DI pipe from the connection to the main to the property line, with a gate valve at the connection to the main and a backflow preventer inside the property line accessible for inspection by City personnel

WWP-33.1.deficiency: Water mains do not maintain minimum 48-inch depth of cover measured from the uppermost pipe projection to proposed ground elevation.

WWP-33.2.deficiency: Water mains exceed the maximum 72-inch depth of cover limit established by Austin Water operational standards, compromising valve operability and constructability, and AW review and approval has not been obtained for the depth exceedance.

WWP-33.3.deficiency: Fire lines or fire hydrant lead service lines do not maintain minimum 48-inch depth of cover per UCM 2.9.2.B.4; profile does not verify adequate depth of cover, proper grade, and clearance from other utilities.

WWP-33.4.deficiency: Reclaimed water lines do not maintain minimum 48-inch depth of cover below proposed ground elevation.

WWP-33.5.deficiency: Valve operating nuts are not set between 12 and 24 inches below finished grade. (This is a distinct requirement from the 48-inch pipe cover minimum; plan notes must not conflate the two.)

WWP-33.6.deficiency: Wastewater mains in easements or undeveloped areas do not maintain minimum 42-inch depth of cover below proposed ground elevation.

WWP-33.7.deficiency: Wastewater mains in streets or traffic areas do not maintain minimum 66-inch depth of cover below proposed ground elevation. "Traffic areas" includes proposed and existing streets, private drives, access roads, parking and loading areas, and areas subject to maintenance equipment operation.

WWP-33.8.deficiency: Wastewater service lines and cleanouts do not provide 4 to 6 feet of cover as required by Austin Water Standard Detail 520-AW-01C and UCM 2.9.4.G.1.

WWP-33.9.deficiency: Wastewater mains in streets where the 66-inch minimum depth of cover cannot be achieved do not have a formal waiver request submitted to Austin Water and AW approval has not been obtained.

WWP-33.10.deficiency: Steel encasement is not provided where a water main (potable or reclaimed) or fire line crosses beneath a wastewater main, as required by UCM 2.9.1.B.3.

WWP-33.11.deficiency: Steel encasement at a water/wastewater crossing is less than 18 feet in length, or the encasement is not centered on the wastewater main.

WWP-33.12.deficiency: Steel encasement at a water/wastewater crossing does not use full-circumferential welded joints; cement-stabilized sand, PVC, HDPE, concrete, or other substitute materials are not permitted.

WWP-33.13.deficiency: Minimum 12-inch vertical clearance between the existing wastewater main and the top of the water pipe is not maintained within the steel encasement.

WWP-33.14.deficiency: Steel encasement piping less than 24 inches in diameter does not extend a minimum of 3 feet beyond adjacent appurtenances; encasement 24 inches or larger does not extend a minimum of 5 feet beyond adjacent appurtenances.

WWP-33.15.deficiency: For HDD (Horizontal Directional Drill) trenchless crossings of potable, reclaimed water, or wastewater force mains, the HDPE casing pipe is not specified as two nominal pipe sizes larger than the HDPE carrier pipe; or the crossing detail does not specify spacers, pipe joint restraint, and factory end seals as required for encased installations.

WWP-33.16.deficiency: Plan details at water/wastewater crossings do not show all required elements to demonstrate TCEQ compliance, including vertical alignment, depth of cover, encasement termination details, spacers, pipe joint restraint, and factory end seals.

WWP-33.17.deficiency: At water/wastewater crossings, the crossing detail does not include a plan note requiring a full stick of pipe (minimum 18 feet) centered over the wastewater line to ensure no pipe joints occur at or adjacent to the crossing, as required by TCEQ 217.53(d)(5)(B) and UCM 2.9.1.B.1.

WWP-33.18.deficiency: Trenchless installations beneath existing water lines do not maintain a minimum vertical clearance of 36 inches or twice the excavation diameter or span (whichever is larger), measured from the outside surface of the water line to the top of the trenchless excavation.

WWP-33.19.deficiency: Trenchless installations within 10 feet horizontally of a water line do not specify continuous support of the advancing excavation face and crown at all times.

WWP-33.20.deficiency: Bore or trenchless crossing plan details do not include a project-specific Special Detail depicting all required elements: bore path alignment, launch and receiving pit locations and dimensions, and casing and carrier pipe specifications.

WWP-33.21.deficiency: A bore crossing installation results in less than 30 inches of cover over the bore pipe, and no notification to the Engineer has been documented and no concrete seal, cradle, cap, or encasement has been specified as required.

WWP-33.22.deficiency: Water meter, service, or compound/master meter vault depth exceeds 72 inches from finished grade to vault floor, or the vault does not maintain minimum 48-inch cover over the uppermost pipe projection; AW review and approval has not been documented for vault depth outside this range.

WWP-33.23.deficiency: A minimum 5-foot exclusive clearance zone around and under vault structures is not maintained; other utilities, appurtenances, or structures (except associated irrigation services) are present within this zone on any side of the vault, not only below it.

WWP-33.24.deficiency: Vault depth is not clearly dimensioned on profile views, making it impossible to verify compliance with cover and depth requirements.

WWP-33.25.deficiency: Fire lines entering and passing through vaults are not installed at zero slope (level installation required); slope or grade is annotated on vault profile or fire line detail sheets.

WWP-33.26.deficiency: External drop connections are shown for wastewater mains larger than 15 inches in diameter, or at depths exceeding 15 feet from the manhole lid to the base of the manhole, in violation of UCM 2.9.4.D.6.

WWP-33.27.deficiency: Drop connections exceeding 15 feet in depth from lid to base are not designed as internal drops using a minimum 5-foot-diameter manhole as required.

WWP-33.28.deficiency: Profile views do not show depth-of-cover dimensions and calculations at critical locations (e.g., crossings, low points, transitions, areas of minimum cover) to demonstrate compliance with applicable requirements.

WWP-33.29.deficiency: Existing utility depths at critical crossing and connection locations are annotated only as "per record drawings" or "per as-builts" (QL-D quality) without physical exposure (vacuum excavation / QL-A) data; while field investigation is encouraged per UCM 2.5.1.E.10, QL-A data is expected at utility conflict points per UCM 3.3.4 and 3.7.2.

WWP-33.30.deficiency: Where substandard depth-of-cover conditions exist, the deficiency has not been documented with supporting calculations and Austin Water approval has not been obtained.

WWP-33.31.deficiency: Duct banks for dry utilities are placed over existing wastewater lines, blocking maintenance access.

WWP-33.32.deficiency: Trench integrity is not maintained for water or wastewater utility infrastructure; shared trenching or trench overlap between utility types prevents independent maintenance and operation.

WWP-33.33.deficiency: Water line trenches specify CLSM (flowable fill) for the entire trench length, rather than limiting CLSM to the utility crossing zone (beneath and within 5 feet horizontally of the water main); engineered backfill per COA Standard Specifications is required for the remainder of the trench.

WWP-33.34.deficiency: Pipe bedding envelope does not extend 6 inches below the pipe bottom and 12 inches above the pipe top (full trench width) as required; or the specified bedding material does not match the applicable standard for the pipe type.

WWP-33.35.deficiency: Where open cut is proposed under or adjacent to an existing water main consisting of asbestos cement (AC) pipe or cast-iron (CI) pipe with lead caulk joints, the main has not been designated for removal and replacement, and no design detail showing how the main will be supported during construction has been provided; note that this requirement applies only when the trench under the water main is 3 feet or less in width.

WWP-33.36.deficiency: Valve casings for abandoned water mains are not specified to be removed to the top of the subgrade or 24 inches below the surface (whichever is greater), with the remaining casing filled with concrete so the abandoned valve is not identifiable from the surface.

WWP-33.37.deficiency: Embankment is not specified to be constructed to at least 1 foot above the top of the utility before excavating the utility trench, for utilities installed beneath proposed embankment.

WWP-33.38.deficiency: Proposed pipe segments at utility crossings are not centered over the centerline of the crossed utility, or the crossing detail does not include a note requiring centering of the pipe segment at the crossing per TCEQ requirements.

WWP-33.39.deficiency: Irrigation distribution piping within a retention/irrigation stormwater water quality system is not buried at sufficient depth to protect it from weather, vandalism, and vehicular traffic including maintenance equipment.

WWP-33.40.deficiency: Water or reclaimed water mains crossing under TxDOT ROW, railroad ROW, or any flowing, intermittent, or semi-permanent stream do not include a plan note conforming to current COA Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ) crossing criteria, and/or the crossing profile does not demonstrate that the pipe invert is at least 1 foot below the calculated subsurface EHZ geometry per DCM Appendix E Step 7A; or the required encasement pipe, drain valve at the low point, and isolation valves with CAV on each side are not shown.

WWP-33.41.deficiency: Reclaimed water mains are shown at depths substantially exceeding the 48-inch minimum without documentation of Austin Water approval for the maximum depth, as required for the specific materials, application, and site conditions.

WWP-33.42.deficiency: Fill or embankment placed over existing water, reclaimed water, or wastewater mains or services exceeds 4 feet above existing ground elevation, or results in a final depth exceeding twice the easement width, without Austin Water review and approval documented in the plan set.

WWP-34.1.deficiency: Joint restraint type and beginning/ending station limits not annotated in the plan view for restrained segments

WWP-34.2.deficiency: Joint restraint type and station locations not annotated in the profile view for restrained segments

WWP-34.3.deficiency: Generic "RESTRAIN ALL JOINTS" note used without specific restraint type, beginning/ending station limits, or reference to City of Austin standards; note must reference COA standards and provide specific calculated restraint extents

WWP-34.4.deficiency: Joint restraint calculations not provided for water main segments with bends, deflections, or horizontal curves; calculations are required to document the minimum 1.5 safety factor and establish station limits

WWP-34.5.deficiency: Joint restraint calculations do not demonstrate the minimum required safety factor of 1.5

WWP-34.6.deficiency: Burial depth used in restraint calculations does not match actual burial depths shown on profile sheets; generic assumed depth (e.g., 4 feet) used in lieu of actual profile-derived depths

WWP-34.7.deficiency: Pipe material properties not correctly applied in restraint calculations; ductile iron (DI) and PVC C-900 have different joint restraint behavior and must not be interchanged in the same calculation template

WWP-34.8.deficiency: Actual specified bedding material type not used in restraint length calculations; bedding material (cement stabilized backfill, sand, pea gravel, or pipe bedding stone per SSM Item No. 510s.3) affects thrust resistance and must match the material specified on plans

WWP-34.9.deficiency: Joint restraint at street intersections does not extend to at least the point of curvature (PC) of the curb line

WWP-34.10.deficiency: Horizontal curve data not provided (radius, arc length, chord length, delta angle, PC and PT stations) as required for all water and reclaimed water plans; this data is necessary to verify joint deflection limits are not exceeded

WWP-34.11.deficiency: Concrete thrust blocking proposed for a water or reclaimed water main without documented case-by-case Austin Water approval; mechanical joint restraint is the required standard and thrust blocking is the exception requiring explicit AW approval

WWP-34.12.deficiency: Concrete thrust blocking proposed within the downtown thrust blocking prohibition area (Loop 1/MoPac to IH-35 east-west; Lady Bird Lake to 30th Street north-south); thrust blocking is absolutely prohibited in this area — Austin Water case-by-case approval authority does not apply within this boundary

WWP-34.13.deficiency: Concrete thrust blocking proposed at a dead-end water main; thrust blocking is prohibited at dead-end mains regardless of project location or Austin Water approval

WWP-34.14.deficiency: Austin Water-approved concrete thrust blocking plans do not show specific block dimensions and locations; when thrust blocking is approved, the engineer must include block dimensions, locations, and consideration of proximity to other utilities/structures on the plans

WWP-34.15.deficiency: Joint restraint not provided at pipe bends on water or reclaimed water mains

WWP-34.16.deficiency: Joint restraint not provided at fittings or at locations where joint deflection is utilized on water or reclaimed water mains

WWP-34.17.deficiency: Joint restraint not provided at reducer or tee fittings on reclaimed water mains; UCM 2.9.3.B.10 explicitly requires restraint at reducers and tees for reclaimed water — this requirement is more stringent than the water main standard, which requires restraint at bends and joint deflections only

WWP-34.18.deficiency: Joint restraint gaskets or external mechanical joint restraint devices not specified at mechanical joint (MJ) fittings for DI pipe 24 inches and smaller or for PVC pipe; these are the required restraint device types for these pipe sizes per UCM 2.9.2.B.8

WWP-34.19.deficiency: Integral, factory joint restraint system not specified for DI pipe larger than 24 inches in diameter; external mechanical joint restraint devices are not acceptable for DI pipe greater than 24 inches — integral factory joint restraint systems are required

WWP-34.20.deficiency: Approved HDPE MJ Adapter per applicable AW Standard Products Lists not specified for connections of HDPE pipe to mechanical joint valves and fittings; standard external MJ restraint devices are not acceptable for HDPE-to-MJ connections

WWP-34.21.deficiency: Joint restraint not provided at dead-end conditions, or not provided on both sides of a valve that would create a dead-end condition

WWP-34.22.deficiency: Restrained plug on tee connection does not include both one joint of restrained pipe and a plug with a 1-inch or larger tap; both elements are conjunctively required — the use of "and/or" in plan notes or details misrepresents the code requirement

WWP-34.23.deficiency: External mechanical joint restraint device not specified for restraint at tee connections to DI or PVC pipe; plans may reference "Foster adapter" or other outdated terminology not found in current UCM 2.9.2.B.8 — the current code term is "external mechanical joint restraint devices" for DI/PVC connections

WWP-34.24.deficiency: Correct joint restraint device type not specified for valve connections at encased pipe segments or restrained joint installations; external mechanical joint restraint device required for DI or PVC pipe; approved HDPE MJ Adapter per applicable AW SPLs required for HDPE pipe — "foster adapter" terminology is not current UCM language

WWP-34.25.deficiency: Detailed construction drawings not provided for tee or valve assemblies showing all components, materials, installation sequence, and joint restraint methods; plan view details of appurtenances and supplementary special details are required to clearly convey design intent

WWP-34.26.deficiency: Private fire service (fire line) not fully restrained with joint restraint throughout; restraint is required at all bends and deflections, and both plan and profile views must annotate restraint type and station limits

WWP-34.27.deficiency: Service water line joint restraint not provided from main connection point to the backflow preventer, or restraint type and station limits not annotated in both plan and profile views

WWP-34.28.deficiency: Force main thrust restraint required at bends or fittings but not shown on the plan view; the force main standard requires plan view annotation when thrust restraint is needed but does not independently prescribe a safety factor or profile view annotation (those requirements apply to water mains under UCM 2.9.2.B.9, not force mains)

WWP-34.29.deficiency: Abandoned water main connection does not include a calculated length of restrained pipe on the active main side to prevent thrust displacement when the active main remains pressurized

WWP-34.30.deficiency: Steep water main grade change does not include appropriate joint restraint design to resist longitudinal thrust; steep vertical curves create thrust conditions analogous to horizontal bends requiring calculations and annotation

WWP-34.31.deficiency: Fire hydrant assembly joints not fully restrained throughout all fittings and connections; the entire fire hydrant assembly — including all fittings and the connection to the main — must have restrained joints

WWP-34.32.deficiency: Fire hydrant connection detail does not show hydrant lead size, valve type, and joint restraint method; the hydrant lead valve must be restrained to the main using bolt-through types of connections between the valve and the branch outlet from the main

WWP-34.33.deficiency: Existing Cast Iron or Asbestos Concrete pipe proposed to be connected to or extended is not being removed and replaced with DI pipe or PVC C-900; these pipe materials cannot be mechanically restrained and must be replaced to ensure adequate joint restraint; plans may label these materials as CI, C-I, CIP (Cast Iron) or AC, ACP (Asbestos Concrete)

WWP-34.34.deficiency: Pipes, valves, and/or fittings greater than 2 inches proposed in TxDOT ROW, Austin Bergstrom International Airport (ABIA) property, or University of Texas property are not specified as restrained ductile iron pipe

WWP-35.1.deficiency: Potential sources of industrial waste on the site not identified or acknowledged on plans — check for restaurants, grease traps, tenant car washes, pool backwash to sanitary sewer, trash compactors with floor drains, dumpster compactors with drains, elevator sump connections, and underground parking

WWP-35.2.deficiency: Grease interceptor not shown on utility plans for a proposed food service establishment (restaurant, commercial kitchen, hotel kitchen, fire/EMS station kitchen, convenience store with food prep, or kiosk with non-prepackaged food sales) per §15-10-71

WWP-35.3.deficiency: Multiple food service establishments are proposed but fewer than one grease interceptor per establishment is shown; shared or in-series grease interceptors are permitted only in extreme circumstances (e.g., high-rise building with no outdoor space) and must be justified through a Grease Interceptor Installation Variance Request (GIIVR) form submitted to Austin Water

WWP-35.4.deficiency: Trash room with a floor drain AND a trash compactor is proposed but a minimum 100-gallon grease interceptor is not shown per Industrial Waste requirements; a grit trap is not an acceptable substitute in a trash room

WWP-35.5.deficiency: Future commercial or retail tenants may include food service establishments but no designated space or note for a future grease interceptor is shown on the utility plan; plans must either show a reserved GI location or include a written acknowledgment that every food-service tenant will require a separate GI and that the site can accommodate future modifications

WWP-35.6.deficiency: Grease interceptor location not shown on all applicable utility plan sheets; if the interceptor is located exterior to the building footprint, it must also appear on the site plan

WWP-35.7.deficiency: Inlet pipe and outlet pipe not both shown on plans; plans do not label which pipe is the inlet (influent) and which is the outlet (effluent)

WWP-35.8.deficiency: Size of inlet and outlet piping of the grease interceptor not indicated on plans; size, slope, and material of grease waste piping serving the interceptor not shown

WWP-35.9.deficiency: Cleanouts (2-way cleanouts) associated with the grease interceptor not shown on plans

WWP-35.10.deficiency: How the grease interceptor effluent connects to the downstream sanitary sewer system not shown or clarified; junction of sanitary sewer line and grease waste line downstream of the interceptor not depicted

WWP-35.11.deficiency: Correct device orientation not shown — the larger chamber must be the influent (inlet) chamber and the smaller chamber must be the effluent (outlet) chamber

WWP-35.12.deficiency: Detail box showing grease interceptor configuration, inlet/outlet piping, and sample port not provided when the full device configuration cannot be clearly shown at utility plan scale; detail boundary must include the complete service connection per UCM 2.5.3.A.5 and UCM 2.5.3.A.6

WWP-35.13.deficiency: For a multi-building site, grease interceptor location and associated piping not shown for each individual building that requires one

WWP-35.14.deficiency: Commercial or institutional food preparation facility plans show a food waste disposal (garbage disposal) unit — which is prohibited — or show a dishwasher that is not connected to the grease interceptor; per LDC §25-12-153/1014.1.3, food waste disposal units may not be installed in commercial or institutional food preparation facilities, and dishwashers in such facilities must connect to the GI unless specifically exempted by Austin Water; if MEP/plumbing plans are not included in the SDP submittal, flag for required verification at building permit review stage

WWP-37.23.deficiency: All wastewater from a single water meter must consolidate at one point — with a dedicated sample/inspection port at the property line within the ROW or utility easement — before entering the wastewater easement, per UCM § 2.9.4.G.7 and COA Standard Detail 520S-3A

WWP-37.26.deficiency: Plans must determine and document whether Chapter 15-10 (Industrial Waste Control Program) applies to the project; an IWCP acknowledgment note is required on plans for all projects within Austin Water's service area; residential-only flows may qualify for a § 15-10-98 exemption from the IWDP permit requirement only if the director affirmatively determines all qualifying conditions are met — designers cannot self-certify the exemption

WWP-37.36.deficiency: Direct connection to a wastewater main larger than 15 inches in diameter is prohibited per UCM § 2.9.4.G.3; standard wastewater main sizes jump from 15 inches directly to 18 inches (no standard 16- or 17-inch sizes), making this effectively a prohibition on service connections to wastewater interceptors (generally ≥18 inches per LDC § 25-9-32(14)); connection to an interceptor also requires a WWSER per LDC § 25-9-33(A)(2)

WWP-37.39.deficiency: Construction — including utility line installation — is prohibited within the 150-foot CEF buffer per LDC § 25-8-281(C)(2)(b); utility lines are not among the limited exceptions (hiking trails, approved recharge basins, § 25-8-151 innovative management practices) permitted at ≥50 feet from the CEF edge; routing wastewater within a CEF buffer requires documentation of either an administrative variance from WPD per § 25-8-42 or a Land Use Commission variance per § 25-8-41; plans showing utilities within a CEF buffer without variance documentation are deficient
