WWP-41.5.deficiency: Fire line pipe sizes shown on one plan sheet (e.g., site utility plan, water plan & profile, demand table, AW General Note Sheet, or engineer's response letter) differ from sizes shown on another sheet or document for the same segment

WWP-41.6.deficiency: Wastewater pipe sizes shown on one plan sheet (e.g., overall utility plan, wastewater collection plan, wastewater plan & profile, DFU table, or building-scale utility plan) differ from sizes shown on another sheet for the same segment

WWP-41.7.deficiency: Water utility callout notes or piping notes specify a pipe size, fitting size, or fitting type that is inconsistent with the piping layout shown on the same plan sheet — including tees, reducers, bends, crosses, service taps, and service size callouts (note: PVC is not manufactured in 5/8"; service callouts specifying 5/8" PVC must be revised to an available material/size per COA Standard Details)

WWP-41.8.deficiency: Pipe material specifications in water utility callout notes, general notes, or project utility notes conflict with material specifications shown in other callouts, profiles, or detail sheets for the same utility (e.g., one note specifies C-900 DR14 PVC while another specifies HDPE; utility note specifies DI for all lines 12" and smaller while a callout specifies copper). A common source of this deficiency is carrying project utility notes forward from prior projects without updating the material designation.

WWP-41.9.deficiency: Wastewater callout notes or piping notes specify a pipe size or fitting size that is inconsistent with the piping layout shown on the same or adjacent plan sheets — including callout-to-layout conflicts, piping note-to-callout conflicts, and fitting-to-pipe size mismatches (caps, reducers, couplings, service taps, transitions)

WWP-41.10.deficiency: Wastewater pipe material specifications in callout notes conflict with material specifications shown elsewhere in the plan set (e.g., SDR-26 PVC vs. Schedule 40 PVC; PVC vs. concrete shown in profile). Per SSM 510.2(l), all PVC wastewater pipe in the 6–15-inch range (ASTM D 3034) must be SDR-26 or better — a conflict that includes any callout showing SDR-35 or an undesignated "PVC" is a deficiency regardless of other material designations.

WWP-41.11.deficiency: Orifice or control structure opening dimensions called out on the plan view, detail sheets, or in the sizing calculations contain conflicting values or do not correspond to the hydraulic model sizing (e.g., orifice called out as 0.61-inch diameter in one location and 0.8-inch in another; outfall orifice dimensioned as 6"×9" in one location and 6"×8.5" in another)

WWP-41.12.deficiency: Wastewater manhole inlet/outlet count shown in callout notes does not match the number of pipe connections illustrated in the plan drawing for the same manhole

WWP-41.13.deficiency: Wye fitting inlet/outlet orientation is incorrectly described in callout notes — wye fittings have two inlets and one outlet; callout notes describing a wye as having one inlet and two outlets must be corrected

WWP-41.14.deficiency: Private wastewater piping shows a prohibited pipe size reduction — the pipe diameter decreases in the direction of flow, which violates the Uniform Plumbing Code (adopted by reference per LDC § 25-12-151(A))

WWP-41.15.deficiency: Wastewater service branch piping diameter is undersized relative to the connected building demand, or creates a throttling condition where a smaller service connects to a larger building stub (e.g., 8" residential service connecting to a 12" building stub with potential flow restriction). UCM 2.9.4.G.2 requires wastewater service lines to have an inside diameter of not less than 6 inches; DFU-based sizing per BCM § 5.6.1.C.2 may require a larger diameter depending on total fixture unit load.

WWP-41.16.deficiency: The private (non-City O&M) lift station sectional elevation view specifies discharge assembly components at 2-inch diameter instead of the required 3-inch minimum per AW Wastewater Lift Station General Specifications — components to check include: force main piping, discharge piping, Schedule 80 PVC flanges, threaded plug valves, bolt-on couplings, Schedule 80 PVC male adapters, Schedule 80 PVC unions, and stainless steel rail pipes. For lift stations proposed for Austin Water O&M acceptance (public), UCM 2.9.4.J.7.b requires a 4-inch minimum force main regardless of the private system standard.

WWP-41.17.deficiency: The break-away fitting model specified for the private lift station is a 2-inch configuration (e.g., BAF-2020) that is incompatible with the required 3-inch discharge assembly; only BAF-1212 or BAF-1220 are acceptable for a 3-inch system per AW Wastewater Lift Station General Specifications

WWP-41.18.deficiency: The force main diameter specified in the lift station plan view, sectional elevation, or detail sheet conflicts with the force main diameter shown on the utility plans or wastewater plan (e.g., plan view shows 2" or 4" while wastewater plan shows 3" or 6"). For private lift stations, the minimum force main diameter is 3 inches per AW Wastewater Lift Station General Specifications; for public lift stations proposed for City O&M acceptance, UCM 2.9.4.J.7.b requires a 4-inch minimum.

WWP-41.19.deficiency: The lift station sump inlet size shown in the lift station plan view conflicts with the sump inlet size shown in the utility layout plans

WWP-41.20.deficiency: Pipe length callout values on plan or profile sheets do not match the length derivable from the stationing endpoints, the scale measurement, or the length shown in the profile view for the same segment — includes dimension callouts in detail enlargements and meter details that do not match field-verified or computed measurements

WWP-41.21.deficiency: Pipe slope or grade callout values conflict with the slope derivable from the pipe invert elevations shown in the profile view, or conflict with the slope shown in piping notes or callout notes for the same segment

WWP-41.22.deficiency: Utility separation dimension callouts are not measured outside-diameter (OD) to outside-diameter (OD), or the called-out dimension value does not match the drawn separation shown in the plan. UCM 2.9.1.B.1 explicitly requires all separation distances to be measured OD to OD — a common violation is labeling center-to-center or wall-to-wall distances, which is especially significant for large-diameter pipes where the OD substantially exceeds the nominal size.

WWP-41.23.deficiency: Callout notes contain placeholder "##" values instead of actual sheet numbers — all placeholder references must be replaced with the correct sheet number before approval

WWP-41.24.deficiency: Callout notes reference sheet numbers that either do not exist in the plan set or point to a sheet containing unrelated content (e.g., multiple callouts reference "Sheet 353" which is the Detention Pond Plan rather than the intended utility content)

WWP-41.25.deficiency: Callout notes reference details, profiles, or notes that do not exist on the referenced sheet or anywhere else in the plan set — includes references to "note 1 on this sheet" where no such note exists, and references to utility profile sheets for lines not shown in any profile

WWP-41.26.deficiency: Utilities continuing across sheet boundaries do not include cross-reference notes identifying the continuation sheet — or existing cross-reference notes reference incorrect sheet numbers. Per UCM 2.5.1.E.19, utilities spanning three or more plan-and-profile sheets require an Overall Location Map and Key Map on each affected sheet. Austin Water reviewer convention additionally requires a cross-reference note at each sheet boundary where a utility continues, identifying the continuation sheet number; a violation is visible when a utility line ends at a sheet edge without any reference box, or when the reference box cites a sheet number that does not continue the utility.

WWP-41.27.deficiency: Utility designation (existing utility to remain, existing utility to be removed, or proposed utility) shown on the demolition plan is inconsistent with the designation shown on the utility plan for the same utility segment — includes situations where one sheet shows a utility proposed for removal while another shows it as remaining

WWP-41.28.deficiency: Construction phasing shown for utilities or buildings on one plan sheet is inconsistent with phasing shown on another plan sheet — e.g., an overall private water plan shows three buildings in the background while all other plan sheets show only two buildings for the same phase

WWP-41.29.deficiency: Building footprints, orientations, or building identification numbers shown on one plan sheet (e.g., site plan, utility plan, or architectural sheet) are inconsistent with what is shown on another plan sheet for the same buildings — includes referenced architectural sheets that are incomplete or marked "for review only" rather than fully sealed

WWP-41.30.deficiency: On-site water reuse system (OWRS) locations shown on MEP building plan sheets do not match OWRS locations shown on the site utility plan sheets, or conflicting OWRS sheets are included in the plan set without reconciliation. An OWRS collects and treats non-potable water sources (condensate, rainwater, graywater, stormwater, foundation drain) for non-potable uses; OWRS is mandatory for projects with GFA ≥ 250,000 SF (multi-family/mixed-use/commercial, site plan application on or after April 1, 2024) per LDC § 25-9-414.

WWP-41.31.deficiency: A water main size specified in the plan or profile is not in the list of allowable water main sizes per UCM 2.9.2.B.10 (e.g., 5-inch, 14-inch, or 18-inch, which are not on the allowable list) and no AW case-by-case approval is documented

WWP-41.32.deficiency: A gravity wastewater main size specified in the plan or profile is not in the list of allowable gravity wastewater pipe sizes per UCM 2.9.4.B.6 (e.g., 10-inch or 14-inch, which are not on the allowable list) and no AW case-by-case approval is documented

WWP-41.33.deficiency: The wastewater profile view is missing required flow data — peak dry weather flow (PDWF), peak wet weather flow (PWWF), and/or associated design velocities are absent for one or more pipe segments — or the stated design velocity for a segment is inconsistent with the stated pipe slope and diameter (e.g., the called-out velocity cannot be produced by the labeled percent grade under Manning's equation for the given pipe size)

WWP-42.1.deficiency: Water Balance Calculator is not the current version — applicant reused a prior submittal's file rather than downloading a fresh copy from Austin Water's Onsite Water Reuse web page

WWP-42.2.deficiency: Water Balance Calculator contains red text — calculation errors or invalid entries have not been resolved before submission; a WBC with unresolved formula errors is not a "completed" Water Benchmarking Application

WWP-42.3.deficiency: Page 9 (Follow-up Survey / Water Benchmarking Dashboard) of the Water Benchmarking Application not completed — one or more required questions left unanswered

WWP-42.4.deficiency: OWRS (Onsite Water Reuse System) operating permit application submitted outside Austin Water's designated submission channel — Austin Water's standard submittal platform is the AB+C Portal (Austin Build + Connect); submission by email or other informal channel is not accepted by Austin Water

WWP-42.5.deficiency: Water Benchmarking Application not submitted for a project that revises or extends an existing site — applicant incorrectly asserts that revisions or extensions are exempt from WBC; no such exemption exists

WWP-42.6.deficiency: WBC does not include all existing and proposed buildings shown on the site plan — one or more buildings omitted from benchmarking inputs

WWP-42.7.deficiency: Site Area value in WBC does not match the gross site area shown on the site plan application

WWP-42.8.deficiency: Building Coverage value in WBC does not match Building Coverage reported in the Site Plan Data Table

WWP-42.9.deficiency: Gross site area on the plan set does not match the gross site area indicated on the final plat

WWP-42.10.deficiency: When an Engineering Summary Letter (ESL) is provided: site area or development area stated in the ESL is inconsistent with the WBC and the limits of construction shown on plans

WWP-42.11.deficiency: When an ESL states a percentage of the site available for development (e.g., "100% of site area available"): that percentage is inconsistent with the limits of construction depicted on the plan set

WWP-42.12.deficiency: Gross Floor Area (GFA) in the WBC includes parking or garage areas — these must be excluded per Austin Water application instructions

WWP-42.13.deficiency: Gross Floor Area (GFA) in the Site Coverage or Building Information sections of the WBC includes unconditioned areas (e.g., open breezeways, unenclosed structures) — must be excluded

WWP-42.14.deficiency: Project Type incorrectly selected in the WBC — must reflect actual composition of the development (Residential, Commercial, Mixed Use, or Office)

WWP-42.15.deficiency: Use types selected in the WBC Building Information section do not match the proposed uses on the site plan or project data table

WWP-42.16.deficiency: Hotel with additional uses not designated as "Lodging" in the WBC Building Information section — lodging must be the primary use type when hotel is present

WWP-42.17.deficiency: Non-standard building components such as clubhouses or maintenance buildings not included in the WBC Building Information section with their corresponding Gross Floor Area

WWP-42.18.deficiency: Commercial use within Live/Work units or other mixed-use buildings not reflected in the WBC as a separate use type with its own square footage

WWP-42.19.deficiency: WBC Building Information section missing total bedroom count breakdown or unit type designations for residential buildings

WWP-42.20.deficiency: Commercial or Education GFA fields in the WBC do not match the corresponding GFA values on the site plan or project data table

WWP-42.21.deficiency: HVAC/AC system capacity not entered (or entered in wrong units) under the "Other Water Use Information" section of the WBC — capacity must be expressed in tons

WWP-42.22.deficiency: Cooling Tower question response under "Other Water Use Information" is incorrect, blank, or inconsistent with the proposed mechanical systems

WWP-42.23.deficiency: Number of employees or number of students listed in the WBC is unconfirmed, incorrect, or inconsistent with the project program

WWP-42.24.deficiency: Residential Appliance and Amenity Information values in the WBC not updated after the total number of residential units changed from a prior submittal

WWP-42.25.deficiency: Project Information or AW Infrastructure Table missing one or more required fields — incomplete entries left blank or filled with placeholder values

WWP-42.26.deficiency: AW Infrastructure table items improperly categorized — infrastructure elements assigned to wrong type classification (e.g., fire suppression listed as domestic, public listed as private)

WWP-42.27.deficiency: AW Infrastructure table data not reconciled with the Engineering Report — discrepancies between table entries and report narrative or calculations

WWP-42.28.deficiency: RSMP Application Form Site Area field populated with the limit of construction area rather than the actual gross site area — RSMP participation fees are calculated on actual site area; using the limit of construction area understates the fee

WWP-42.29.deficiency: Large development project submitted for site plan release without documentation of a pre-release director consultation meeting — LDC § 25-9-413(B) requires that for projects with total GFA ≥ 250,000 SF, the applicant must meet with the Austin Water director prior to site plan release to discuss water efficiency code requirements, benchmarking data, and available incentives/rebates

WWP-42.30.deficiency: Site plan submitted for release without Austin Water director approval of the Water Benchmarking Application — director approval is a mandatory condition of site plan approval under LDC § 25-9-413(A)(2)(b); the site plan may not be released before this approval is obtained

WWP-42.31.deficiency: Site plan for a large development project (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) does not include the signed "SP OWRS Acknowledgement" sheet from the approved Water Balance Calculator — this sheet is required in the site plan set to document OWRS compliance for large development projects

WWP-42.32.deficiency: Project's property boundary is within the mandatory reclaimed water connection distance threshold but the site plan does not show a reclaimed water connection — small development projects (GFA < 250,000 SF) must connect when within 250 ft of a reclaimed water line; large development projects (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) must connect when within 500 ft; when connected, reclaimed water must be used for irrigation, cooling, toilet flushing, and other significant non-potable uses identified in the WBC

WWP-43.1.deficiency: All water utility lines must be labeled with Austin Water GIS asset ID numbers or intersection numbers

WWP-43.2.deficiency: All GIS/intersection numbers shown on plans must be verified against Austin Water's asset management system — inaccurate numbers must be corrected and replaced with numbers confirmed from AW records

WWP-43.3.deficiency: Water service locations and water stub locations must be verified against Austin Water tap records and as-built GIS data, and corrected where plan locations are inaccurate

WWP-43.4.deficiency: Replace all instances of "City Public Works," "Public Works," or similar non-AW department names with "Austin Water" throughout the plan set, including General Notes, approval blocks, and all applicable notes

WWP-43.5.deficiency: Use the official department name "Austin Water" (not "Austin Water Utility") in approval signature blocks and department references throughout the plan set

WWP-43.6.deficiency: Do not label water meters as "private meters" — water meters are Austin Water property and public utility assets regardless of the use they serve or their location on private property

WWP-43.7.deficiency: Plans must clearly distinguish between public water lines (owned and maintained by Austin Water) and private water lines (owned and maintained by the property owner)

WWP-43.8.deficiency: Potable and non-potable water systems must be labeled and identified separately — reclaimed water lines must use the "RECLAIMED WATER" designation and be distinguished from potable water lines per UCM 2.9.3; non-potable piping for OWRS must use purple Schedule 40 PVC with detectable tape labeling per ECM 1.6.7.A; note that UPC Sections 601.3.1 through 601.3.4 are deleted from Austin's adopted plumbing code by LDC § 25-12-151(B) and may not be cited as authority

WWP-43.9.deficiency: Plan notes must not characterize Austin Water as a franchise utility — Austin Water is a municipal utility; remove "WATER," from general notes that list franchise utilities

WWP-43.10.deficiency: Site Plan Release Notes must specify the correct water and wastewater service provider as "Austin Water" and remove any conditional placeholder language such as "(or identify service provider if other than the City of Austin)"

WWP-43.11.deficiency: Replace "SERVICE SADDLE TAP" callouts with "SERVICE SADDLE" to conform to City of Austin standard terminology

WWP-43.12.deficiency: Replace "SER #" with "Connection #" in the LUE Tracking Table labels

WWP-43.13.deficiency: Do not specify domestic meter type as "POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT" in meter callouts or specifications — consult Austin Water for the appropriate meter type designation

WWP-43.14.deficiency: Add the note "AUSTIN WATER CONSTRUCTION NOTES SUPERCEDE ALL OTHER NOTES" directly under the WATER AND WASTEWATER section heading

WWP-43.15.deficiency: Add note: "Do not concrete or pave over Austin Water appurtenances" — appurtenance covers must be adjusted to final grade or pavement must be designed with adequate maintenance clearances

WWP-43.16.deficiency: Trench pavement restoration must be specified in construction notes: water line trenches must be restored with either 4 inches of HMAC or 8 inches of flexible base, consistent with Austin Water General Note Sheet standards; trench thickness values must be consistent throughout the plan set

WWP-43.17.deficiency: Add general note: "UTILITY SERVICE INSTALLATION SHALL COMPLY WITH CITY OF AUSTIN'S UTILITIES CRITERIA MANUAL AND APPLICABLE AMERICAN WATER WORKS STANDARDS"

WWP-43.18.deficiency: The utility verification warning note must use the exact current City of Austin standard Water and Wastewater construction note language — custom supplemental warning language is not permitted

WWP-43.19.deficiency: When project scope does not include any addition or modification to Austin Water infrastructure, add a clarifying callout on the cover sheet and the applicable site plan sheet stating "No Austin Water infrastructure will be changed or modified in any way on this plan set"

WWP-43.20.deficiency: All-weather access roads providing maintenance access to Austin Water facilities must be preserved; construction plans must not remove such roads

WWP-43.21.deficiency: General notes must reference "FIRE HYDRANTS" not "PRIVATE HYDRANTS"

WWP-43.22.deficiency: If private fire hydrants are included on the project, the City of Austin Water and Wastewater Utility Special Services Division note (including the total count of private hydrants) must appear on BOTH the cover sheet AND the utility sheet

WWP-43.23.deficiency: "PRIVATE" designation must be used on fire hydrant callouts only for hydrants physically located on private property; remove "PRIVATE" designation from hydrant callouts for hydrants that are on public property or connected to the public water system but not physically on private property

WWP-43.24.deficiency: All existing fire hydrants must be labeled with their City of Austin GIS identification numbers

WWP-43.25.deficiency: All fire hydrant GIS identification numbers on plans must be verified as accurate against Austin Water database records; discrepancies between hydrant locations on the utility plan and the Austin Water GIS map must be resolved

WWP-43.26.deficiency: Designated space for the Austin Water expiration stamp must be reserved on plan sheets — utility construction must be initiated within three years of plan approval per UCM 2.5.1.A, which is the direct authority for the AW expiration stamp (LDC § 25-5-81(B) governs general site plan expiration but is not the specific authority for the AW utility construction stamp)

WWP-43.27.deficiency: Austin Water sign-off/signature line must appear on the cover sheet (below the professional engineer signature block) to document departmental approval

WWP-43.28.deficiency: City of Austin Water and Wastewater Utility Special Services Division signature block must appear on BOTH the cover sheet AND all utility sheets

WWP-43.29.deficiency: Austin Water contact information (TAPS office address and phone number) must be current and accurate throughout the plan set

WWP-43.30.deficiency: Austin Water project number in the title block must be verified with Austin Water Utility Development Services for accurate project tracking

WWP-43.31.deficiency: Obsolete Service Extension Request (SER) numbers must be removed from the AW General Information Sheet when the associated UIRs or approvals have been processed; only active, applicable SER references should appear

WWP-43.32.deficiency: Infrastructure to be constructed by another project must be labeled on applicable plan sheets as "to be done by others" (or "Proposed to be done by others") and must include the other project's name, Austin Water project number, and SER number

WWP-43.33.deficiency: When a project has multiple associated case numbers providing infrastructure, all applicable case numbers must be listed by project name, Austin Water project number, and SER number in the conditional notes

WWP-43.34.deficiency: Description of Improvements section must clearly identify which infrastructure sections are being completed under this project and which are being completed by other projects, including the other project's name and AW project number

WWP-43.35.deficiency: A letter from the property owner accepting the "CONDITIONS FOR METER RELEASE" section must be provided and placed on the AW General Notes Sheet

WWP-43.36.deficiency: Austin Water Pressure Zone designation must use the full, correct pressure zone name — abbreviations alone are not sufficient

WWP-43.37.deficiency: Austin Water Utility MAPSCO map grid number and City of Austin grid number must both appear on the Vicinity Map

WWP-43.38.deficiency: Austin Water Fire Flow Map reference number (REF#) and date must be documented on the AW sheet and verified to be current and from an authoritative Austin Water source

WWP-43.39.deficiency: The Automated Metering Infrastructure (AMI) section of the AW sheet must confirm that all new water meters, meter boxes, and meter box lids conform to Austin Water's AMI technology and the Standard Products List; the AMI section must document DCU coverage status and acknowledge the applicant's obligation to provide AMI infrastructure extension support, including an easement to the City, poles or structures for Data Collection Units (DCUs), and electrical service to DCUs where solar power is not practical; Austin Water (not the applicant) determines DCU location and performs installation

WWP-43.40.deficiency: If an Onsite Water Reuse System (OWRS) is proposed, the approved OWRS Meter Demand Sheet must be included in the AW Notes Sheet, and the signed SP OWRS Acknowledgement must be submitted to AW_Onsitereuse@austintexas.gov

WWP-43.41.deficiency: When reclaimed water service infrastructure is proposed (whether or not OWRS is also proposed), a Reclaimed Water Meter Demand Sheet must be included in the AW Notes Sheet as a separate, distinct document from any OWRS Meter Demand Sheet — this is required any time a reclaimed water service connection is proposed

WWP-43.42.deficiency: When an irrigation meter waiver has been approved by Austin Water, a note documenting the waiver approval (including the approving Austin Water representative) must be added to the plans

WWP-44.1.deficiency: Manhole invert elevations do not demonstrate the required minimum elevation difference between inlet and outlet pipe inverts: the elevation difference must be the greatest of (1) grade continuation through the manhole centerline, (2) a 2.5% minimum slope, or (3) a 0.10-foot minimum difference. Whichever produces the maximum elevation difference governs.

WWP-44.2.deficiency: Crown-to-crown matching not achieved or not documented at a wastewater manhole where pipes of different sizes connect (tops/crowns of all pipes must be at the same elevation); deviation not supported by documented advance Austin Water UDS approval.

WWP-44.3.deficiency: Wastewater pipe does not enter the manhole at a 90-degree angle (perpendicular to the manhole wall).

WWP-44.4.deficiency: Angle between incoming and outgoing pipe inverts at a wastewater manhole is less than 90 degrees, causing turbulence, splashing, and solids deposition.

WWP-44.5.deficiency: Invert channel flow direction changes not designed with smooth, long-radius sweeps (sharp angles used instead, resulting in turbulence and eddies).

WWP-44.6.deficiency: Manhole invert detail does not show 4–6 inch straight sections between curved portions and connecting pipe ends.

WWP-44.7.deficiency: Wastewater service line vertex not shown extending 2 inches beyond the centerline of the incoming pipe in manhole invert detail.

WWP-44.8.deficiency: Soffit elevation of an incoming storm drain lateral conduit not at approximately the same elevation as the soffit of the trunk line conduit at the manhole; deviation not supported by an approved waiver.

WWP-44.9.deficiency: Correct headloss method per DCM 5.5.2 Table 5-3 not used for storm drain manhole hydraulic calculations. Case 2 applies only when all four conditions are met (single pipe in/out, equal diameters, deflection <90°, no elevation drop). Case 3 (FHWA HEC-22 latest edition) applies to all other configurations.

WWP-44.10.deficiency: Storm drain maintenance path through manhole does not comply: more than one horizontal bend present, horizontal bend deflection exceeds 45 degrees, or vertical bend deflection exceeds 5 degrees.

WWP-44.11.deficiency: Manhole invert plan view detail not provided for a manhole with three or more connecting pipes.

WWP-44.12.deficiency: Manhole invert plan view detail not provided when two pipes connect to a manhole at an angle other than 180 degrees.

WWP-44.13.deficiency: Manhole invert plan view detail not provided for a manhole where a cast-in-place base will be used.

WWP-44.14.deficiency: Existing manhole invert details not provided when replacing or rehabilitating an existing wastewater manhole.

WWP-44.15.deficiency: Invert plan view detail does not show the minimum 12-inch clearance between the existing pipe inside diameter (ID) and the new core hole ID on the inside manhole wall.

WWP-44.16.deficiency: Invert plan view detail does not show the minimum 7-inch separation between pipe penetration holes in new precast manholes or cast-in-place bases.

WWP-44.17.deficiency: New wastewater manhole not constructed on an existing main does not have a precast base (cast-in-place base is only permitted for manholes constructed on existing mains).

WWP-44.18.deficiency: Manhole construction materials are not corrosion-resistant: manhole is not constructed of polymer concrete, or precast concrete without a corrosion-resistant coating or lining per the Austin Water Standard Products List.

WWP-44.19.deficiency: Precast concrete manhole does not conform to ASTM C 478.

WWP-44.20.deficiency: Manhole rings and covers do not conform to the 32-inch diameter standard for new construction.

WWP-44.21.deficiency: Minor manhole height adjustment uses HDPE rings instead of precast reinforced concrete rings. Note: SSM 506.4.N lists HDPE grade rings (SPL WW-146G) as an approved material, but SSM 506.5.I.2 (the construction method section) explicitly requires precast reinforced concrete rings for minor height adjustments — the construction method section controls.

WWP-44.22.deficiency: Minor manhole adjustment detail does not reference Standard Detail 506S-4.

WWP-44.23.deficiency: Major manhole adjustment detail does not reference Standard Detail 506S-2.

WWP-44.24.deficiency: Wastewater manhole with a 6-foot diameter (over a large main) does not include an eccentric cone per Standard Detail 506S-5 to allow safe access to the invert ledge. Stormwater manholes use eccentric cones; wastewater manholes use concentric cones except over large mains where an eccentric cone is required for invert ledge access.

WWP-44.25.deficiency: Manholes located in unpaved areas do not have bolted, watertight covers. Plans may reference Standard Detail 506S-1 (standard ring and cover) without noting the bolted-cover variant required for unpaved areas.

WWP-44.26.deficiency: Manholes located in the TCEQ Edwards Aquifer Recharge Zone do not have bolted, watertight covers. To determine EARZ applicability: (1) check the Cover Sheet EARZ declaration (required field); (2) check watershed classification for Barton Springs Zone designation; (3) check utility sheets for TCEQ Chapter 213 compliance references. Flag for human verification if the Cover Sheet omits the EARZ declaration and watershed classification does not resolve the question.

WWP-44.27.deficiency: Wastewater manholes located below the groundwater level do not include exterior joint sealing and waterproofing measures (exterior joint wraps and interior liner/coating required).

WWP-44.28.deficiency: Wastewater manholes located within the 100-year floodplain do not include waterproofing measures (exterior joint wraps required).

WWP-44.29.deficiency: Existing brick wastewater manhole not replaced with a code-compliant structure when the proposed development intends to connect to it.

WWP-44.30.deficiency: Austin Water Manhole Inspection Report not provided when new construction ties into an existing wastewater manhole. The report is a companion document (not on plan sheets); check the submittal package for any plan showing a "CONNECT TO EXISTING MH" callout or existing manhole GIS number. A separate inspection report is required for each individual manhole being connected to or rehabilitated.

WWP-44.31.deficiency: Manhole Inspection Report does not assess all required elements: structural integrity, watertightness, and corrosion resistance.

WWP-44.32.deficiency: Inspection report identifies deficiencies (structural damage, leaks, or corrosion) but plans do not show required remediation: lining, coating, or full replacement of the existing manhole.

WWP-44.33.deficiency: Plans do not clearly indicate whether an existing manhole will be retained with a new connection or replaced entirely, which determines whether an inspection report is required.

WWP-44.34.deficiency: Rim and invert elevations for existing manholes shown using COA record drawings or as-built records without field verification; the data source and verification methodology are not documented on the plans.

WWP-44.35.deficiency: Drop manhole type (internal vs. external) not specified on plans.

WWP-44.36.deficiency: External drop manhole depth exceeds the 15-foot maximum; an internal drop configuration is required for drops greater than 15 feet.

WWP-44.37.deficiency: External drop manhole design does not use Standard Detail 506S-8 or 506S-9.

WWP-44.38.deficiency: Internal drop manhole with a drop exceeding 15 feet does not have a minimum 5-foot (60-inch) inside diameter.

WWP-44.39.deficiency: Internal drop manhole does not provide a minimum 4-foot (48-inch) clear space between the drop structure and the manhole wall.

WWP-44.40.deficiency: Drop pipes not specified or shown in the drop manhole detail to prevent splashing and solids deposition.

WWP-44.41.deficiency: Vertical drop pipe material in a wastewater drop manhole is not SDR-26 PVC per the Austin Water Standard Products List. SDR-26 (ASTM D 3034) is the maximum permitted SDR for PVC wastewater pipe in Austin; SDR-35 is not acceptable.

WWP-44.42.deficiency: Drop manhole proposed for use as a sampling or line maintenance point; a separate COA-approved large diameter cleanout (Standard Detail 506S-14) at the edge of the wastewater easement is required instead.

WWP-44.43.deficiency: Horizontal separation between a wastewater manhole and a water main is less than 9 feet, without documentation that the manhole joints have been made watertight using externally applied joint wraps (per UCM 2.9.4.D.8; no equivalent alternatives — "externally applied joint wraps" is the specified method).

WWP-44.44.deficiency: Horizontal distance between an existing manhole and a proposed storm drain structure is less than 36 inches (measured outside edge to outside edge).

WWP-44.45.deficiency: Fire hydrant and storm drain manhole locations do not maintain adequate clearance for both structures. Note: UCM 2.9.2.D.7 identifies consideration of utilities as an advisory design factor for fire hydrant placement.

WWP-44.46.deficiency: Separation distances between manholes and adjacent utilities not clearly dimensioned on plans (dimensions not shown as OD-to-OD measurements).

WWP-44.47.deficiency: Abandoned wastewater manhole not removed to at least 4 feet below grade.

WWP-44.48.deficiency: Abandoned wastewater manhole inlets and outlets not plugged outside the structure, or two-foot long sections of inlet and outlet pipes not cut and removed on the outside of the manhole as required. Plans that show only "plugged at the structure" without the two-foot pipe removal do not comply.

WWP-44.49.deficiency: Void left by abandoned wastewater manhole removal not specified to be filled with stabilized sand per Standard Detail 506S-15.

WWP-44.50.deficiency: Abandoned wastewater manhole not identified on plans with the standard demolition symbol (red 'X').

WWP-44.51.deficiency: Polymer concrete manhole not specified at the point where a wastewater force main discharges into a gravity sewer system. A polymer concrete *construction* manhole is required — a corrosion-resistant lining or coating on a standard precast concrete manhole does not satisfy this requirement. Each force main must have its own dedicated polymer manhole; multiple force mains cannot share a single discharge manhole. Absence of a "POLYMER CONCRETE MH" callout on the plan is the primary indicator.

WWP-44.52.deficiency: Reducer not placed on the force main immediately before it discharges into the polymer manhole at the force main/gravity transition.

WWP-44.53.deficiency: Force main discharge manhole entrance and exit elevations are not equal, causing turbulence at the transition.

WWP-44.54.deficiency: Gravity sewer manhole receiving lift station discharge has an invert elevation set too high to accommodate future gravity connections from the lift station service area.

WWP-45.1.deficiency: Water main bends must not exceed 45 degrees; all bends and elbows must be called out on plans with their degree angles

WWP-45.2.deficiency: Directional changes in water and wastewater piping must be achieved through joint deflection or manufactured fittings only; longitudinal bending of pipe is prohibited

WWP-45.3.deficiency: PVC pipe joint deflection at directional changes must not exceed 1 degree per joint or the manufacturer's maximum, whichever is less

WWP-45.4.deficiency: HDPE pipe cold field bending must maintain a minimum radius of 25× outer diameter for DR11 pipe or 20× outer diameter for DR9 pipe; no DI or HDPE fittings and no mechanical water service clamps may be installed within a bent HDPE section

WWP-45.5.deficiency: Non-PVC, non-HDPE pipe joint deflection at directional changes must not exceed the manufacturer's published maximum limits; deflection callouts must be shown on plans

WWP-45.6.deficiency: Fire hydrant leads must maintain a straight connection from the main to the hydrant to avoid water hammer effects and ensure the entire assembly is restrained; horizontal bends on hydrant leads must be minimized

WWP-45.7.deficiency: A minimum of 5 feet of straight pipe must be provided after the last vertical bend and before vault entry to ensure proper flow conditions

WWP-45.8.deficiency: Manufactured bend fittings must conform to the AW Standard Products List; SPL number must be specified in plans or submittal package

WWP-45.9.deficiency: Curved wastewater mains are prohibited; directional changes must occur at manholes using only straight pipe segments between manholes

WWP-45.10.deficiency: Wastewater connections at manhole inverts must use smooth, long-radius sweeps (sweep elbows or long-radius bends) to minimize turbulence, splashing, and eddies; sharp angular fittings at inverts are not permitted

WWP-45.11.deficiency: Cumulative bends on wastewater service connections must not exceed 45 degrees; grade breaks exceeding allowable joint deflection must be made with approved fittings

WWP-45.12.deficiency: Connections to existing cast iron (CI) or asbestos cement (AC) pipe must use SPL-approved transition couplings; transition couplings must be called out with their SPL number on plans

WWP-45.13.deficiency: Direct connections to bar-wrapped Concrete Steel Cylinder (CSC) pipe (AWWA C303/P303/P381) are prohibited; connections must cut and remove a pipe segment and replace it using DI fittings with steel transition adapters and steel butt straps; plans must include a special detail per UCM 2.5.2.C

WWP-45.14.deficiency: Connections to prestressed Concrete Steel Cylinder (CSC) pipe (AWWA L301/E301) require joint-to-joint removal and replacement of entire pipe segments; replacement must use DI or welded steel pipe with MJPE transition adaptors; direct connections are not permitted; plans must include a special detail per UCM 2.5.2.C

WWP-45.15.deficiency: Cast iron (CI) and asbestos cement (AC) pipe cannot be mechanically restrained; existing CI or AC pipe at or near connection points must be removed and replaced with DI or PVC C-900 pipe of adequate length on each side of the connection to ensure proper joint restraint

WWP-45.16.deficiency: HDPE water main branch connections ≥4" must be closed using an electrofusion coupler per SPL WW-706C; the SPL number must appear in the connection callout

WWP-45.17.deficiency: Junctions between plastic pipe and reinforced concrete pipe (RCP) must occur at a manhole or cleanout; plans must include a detail drawing showing the connection method and whether a manhole is required at the plastic-to-RCP junction

WWP-45.18.deficiency: The method used to connect dissimilar pipe materials must be identified and specified on the plans; where proposed water mains connect to existing CSC water mains, special details are required

WWP-45.19.deficiency: Larger diameter pipe may not discharge into smaller diameter pipe; all pipe diameter transitions must show connecting sizes and materials; a temporary exception may be accepted with supporting calculations

WWP-45.20.deficiency: At trunk-line size transitions, soffit elevations of the upstream and downstream pipes must be approximately the same (the soffit offset may equal the headloss at the structure); if equal soffit elevations cannot be achieved, provide written technical justification and submit a waiver request

WWP-45.21.deficiency: Reducer fittings must be provided at all pipe size change locations; detail drawings must show all fittings, adapters, joint types, and installation sequences at the transition point

WWP-45.22.deficiency: All lines into manholes, including drop connections, must match crown-to-crown elevations where feasible; any deviation from crown-to-crown elevation matching requires advance approval by AW UDS - Pipeline Engineering before plan approval; plans must document that advance approval has been obtained

WWP-45.23.deficiency: Non-standard pipe sizes require written justification; specify only standard commercially available sizes from the allowable size lists (water mains: 4", 6" FH leads/services only, 8", 10" HDPE only, 12", 16", 20" HDPE only, 24", 30", 36", 42"; wastewater gravity: 6" services only, 8", 12", 15", 18", 24", 30", 36", 42")

WWP-45.24.deficiency: No bends, fittings, or directional changes are permitted within steel encasement; the carrier pipe must run straight through the encasement with proper spacers, pipe joint restraint, and factory end seals installed

WWP-45.25.deficiency: Service connections and taps are not permitted within steel encasement; all service connections must be located at least 3 feet beyond either end of the encasement (for encasement <24") or at least 5 feet (for encasement ≥24")

WWP-45.26.deficiency: Steel encasement must begin and end no closer than 3 feet to any adjacent appurtenance or connection for encasement smaller than 24" in diameter; steel encasement 24" in diameter and larger must begin and end no closer than 5 feet from any adjacent appurtenance or connection

WWP-45.27.deficiency: 45-degree bends adjacent to steel encasement must be located outside the applicable encasement setback zone (minimum 3 feet from encasement ends for encasement <24", or 5 feet for encasement ≥24"); verify plans against any additional AW Standard Detail clearance requirements for bends near encasement terminations

WWP-45.28.deficiency: Force mains must be a minimum of 4 inches in diameter and sized so that the flow velocity is between 3 and 6 feet per second at both initial and ultimate development conditions; velocity calculations at both conditions must be submitted

WWP-45.29.deficiency: Force main discharge to the gravity system must conform to current AW Standard Details; plans must show the complete discharge configuration including all reducer fittings, dimensions, and connection method to the receiving manhole

WWP-45.30.deficiency: Force main bends must use sweeping 45-degree configurations to minimize pressure loss and turbulence; sharp angular bends on force mains are not acceptable

WWP-45.31.deficiency: Service connections to force mains larger than 2 inches in diameter are not permitted; service connections to force mains 2 inches or smaller in diameter may be allowed only on a case-by-case basis; saddle taps on force mains are not permitted

WWP-45.32.deficiency: Flow direction arrows must be shown on plan drawings at all wastewater main connections; location, size, and material of all existing and proposed mains and services must be indicated on plans

WWP-45.33.deficiency: Tee fitting callouts must include size in standard format (e.g., "6×6 Tee" or "12"×12" Tee")

WWP-45.34.deficiency: Tap connections must be labeled on plans with connection type and size (e.g., "2" Tap")

WWP-45.35.deficiency: All fittings must be called out on plans with the fitting type identified at each connection point (including 45s, tees, wyes, crosses, etc.)

WWP-45.36.deficiency: Tee connections to existing water mains must be shown in the profile view with connection method, elevations at the connection point, and thrust restraint requirements clearly depicted

WWP-45.37.deficiency: Standard product nomenclature must be used in all callouts (e.g., "Foster Adapter," "Swivel Tee"); coupling type and size must be specified when replacing existing pipe sections at connection points

WWP-45.38.deficiency: A full manufactured pipe segment (18–20 LF per manufacturer standard) must be centered at each utility crossing location; pipe joints must not be located at the crossing point

WWP-45.39.deficiency: In-trench pipe replacement exceeding 141 feet is not acceptable; replacement must use open-cut installation or an approved trenchless method

WWP-45.40.deficiency: Existing pipe condition must be assessed before making connections to deteriorated or poor-condition pipe; repairs and restoration must be shown on plans; TV inspection is required for pipe of unknown or poor condition (e.g., existing arch pipe)

WWP-45.41.deficiency: Force mains must discharge into their own distinct polymer manhole; multiple force mains shall not discharge into a single shared manhole; a conventional concrete or precast concrete manhole at the force main discharge point is not a compliant substitute for a polymer manhole; a manhole must be placed at the discharge point of each force main into a gravity wastewater main

WWP-45.42.deficiency: All HDPE-to-HDPE and HDPE-to-fitting connections on force mains must be fused; mechanical joint connections between HDPE force main components are not permitted

WWP-45.43.deficiency: HDPE MJ adaptors conforming to AW SPL WW-706A must be used to join HDPE force main pipe to valves and ductile iron fittings; the SPL number WW-706A must appear in the callout

WWP-45.44.deficiency: Thermal thrust and Poisson Effects force anchors must be specified at locations where HDPE force mains discharge into manholes or gravity wastewater pipes; anchor locations, type, and installation details must be shown on plans

WWP-45.45.deficiency: Where water mains or force mains transition from HDPE pipe to a different pipe material (DI, PVC, etc.), the HDPE pipe segments must be designed for separate hydrostatic testing by isolation valves or other means; the isolation method must be identified on plans

WWP-46.1.deficiency: Installation detail callouts reference incorrect COA Standard Detail number for the proposed service configuration

WWP-46.2.deficiency: Service clamp or saddle not specified at tap locations, or clamp size does not match the water main diameter

WWP-46.3.deficiency: Multiple service taps on the same water main are spaced less than 3 feet apart

WWP-46.4.deficiency: Service connection to an HDPE water main does not specify the required connection method — connections to HDPE mains must use either a mechanical water service clamp (SPL WW-264) or an electrofusion saddle (SPL WW-706C); a generic "service tap" notation on an HDPE main is not acceptable

WWP-46.5.deficiency: Service connection method (saddle, clamp, corporation stop, fitting type) not referenced to the applicable COA Standard Detail

WWP-46.6.deficiency: Connections to Concrete Steel Cylinder (CSC) mains do not include required special detail sheet. The special detail must identify all six required components: (1) pipe material of existing main; (2) existing pipe joint locations (required for pre-stressed CSC); (3) limits of existing pipe removal and required thrust restraint; (4) identification of all piping components; (5) connection method; and (6) special notes. Bar-wrapped CSC: connect by cutting and DI fittings with steel butt straps. Pre-stressed CSC: remove entire pipe segments and replace with DI or welded steel pipe.

WWP-46.7.deficiency: Service taps or connections placed inside meter vaults

WWP-46.8.deficiency: Standard domestic service tap connection includes non-standard extra fittings (e.g., oversized tees) at the tap point

WWP-46.9.deficiency: Where water lines split into branch services, junction detail does not show tee fittings, gate valves separating each branch, and joint restraint locations

WWP-46.10.deficiency: Domestic water service taps into a fire hydrant lead instead of connecting directly to a water distribution main

WWP-46.11.deficiency: Irrigation water service taps into a fire hydrant lead instead of connecting directly to a water distribution main

WWP-46.12.deficiency: Where both fire and domestic service exist for the same building, fire line does not tee directly from the main or domestic meter is not served from a separate independent service connection

WWP-46.13.deficiency: Domestic and irrigation service lines share a single tap at the water main rather than each having a separate independent tap

WWP-46.14.deficiency: Abandoned water service lines not shown on plans with disconnection methodology and point of disconnection at the corporation stop at the main

WWP-46.15.deficiency: All appurtenances of abandoned water service lines (meters, valves, valve casings, cleanouts) not shown as removed

WWP-46.16.deficiency: Abandoned water mains not shown as physically disconnected and plugged at tees or crosses; valve closure alone is shown as the only abandonment method — valve closure alone is expressly prohibited

WWP-46.17.deficiency: Abandonment detail does not show complete disconnection and appurtenance removal per current code: service lines must be disconnected at the corporation stop at the main, and all valves and appurtenances including the water meter must be physically removed

WWP-46.18.deficiency: Water main sizing does not demonstrate adequate hydraulic capacity and compliance with sizing standards for the intended use

WWP-46.19.deficiency: Minimum operating pressure of 50 psi not demonstrated at the highest-elevation meter location for proposed connections (average day demand)

WWP-46.20.deficiency: Hydraulic modeling not submitted when the proposed connection may affect existing water main capacity, or when required by Austin Water

WWP-46.21.deficiency: Documentation not provided to confirm that connections to dead-end public water mains meet active demand and turnover requirements — dead-end mains must achieve 72-hour water turnover per UCM 2.9.2.B.1

WWP-46.22.deficiency: Cul-de-sac dead-end 4-inch main exception not supported: line is 200 feet or longer, or flush valve is not provided at the dead end

WWP-46.23.deficiency: Dead-end water main does not terminate with a plug or cap that has a 1-inch or larger tap

WWP-46.24.deficiency: Dead-end water main does not include an approved automatic flushing device — dead-end mains must achieve 72-hour water turnover; an automatic flushing device is required until active service demand achieves this on its own

WWP-46.25.deficiency: New water main proposed in the same horizontal alignment or trench as an existing Austin Water line

WWP-46.26.deficiency: Water line relocation does not include the tee connection on the existing main (partial relocation stops short of the tee, leaving an inadequate stub)

WWP-46.27.deficiency: Where stub connection pressure may exceed plumbing code limits, a pressure regulating valve (PRV) is not shown on private property outside all public utility easements

WWP-46.28.deficiency: Service lines cannot be isolated from the main without disrupting main flow — no isolation valve (gate valve) shown between the service tap and the main

WWP-46.29.deficiency: Water main alignment does not follow the required route to achieve system looping or maintain required utility separation

WWP-46.30.deficiency: Constructability not demonstrated for replacement-in-place of water lines in the same alignment while maintaining service to customers

WWP-46.31.deficiency: Water line support plan not provided for suspended water lines — plan must show spacer locations, support intervals, and restraint systems

WWP-46.32.deficiency: Service connection proposed to a wastewater force main larger than 2-inch diameter

WWP-46.33.deficiency: Individual water meter service or fire line proposed for connection to a water transmission main 24 inches or larger in diameter — direct retail service connections to transmission mains are prohibited without a Director-approved exception; a Service Extension Request (SER) is required

WWP-46.34.deficiency: Public/private infrastructure boundary not clearly delineated on plans — the service line from the main to the meter box is public infrastructure; piping downstream of the meter box is private

WWP-46.35.deficiency: Connection 4 inches or larger to an existing public water main uses a tapping sleeve or direct tap method rather than the required cut-in tee — size-on-size taps are not permitted; reconnection to an existing tapping sleeve is prohibited; tapping sleeves on DI or PVC mains require documented case-by-case AW approval

WWP-46.36.deficiency: Connection 4 inches or larger to an existing water main proposes reconnection to an existing tapping sleeve, or proposes a size-on-size tap — both methods are expressly prohibited

WWP-46.37.deficiency: Water line 8 inches or larger not designed to public water main standards — the UCM establishes 8 inches as the minimum nominal main size, meaning all lines 8 inches or larger must comply with public main design requirements including valve spacing, looped system design, and standard detail requirements

WWP-46.38.deficiency: Private service line minimum pipe diameter at the public/private boundary not verified against COA Standard Details for the applicable service size

WWP-46.39.deficiency: Austin Utility Location and Coordination Committee (AULCC) coordination not completed for water main assignments in city streets — coordination is categorically required for all water main extensions in city streets with no linear-footage minimum threshold

WWP-46.40.deficiency: Water main connection point shown on plans does not match the exact location designated in the approved Service Extension Request

WWP-46.41.deficiency: Water main alignments, sizing, and easement requirements from the approved Service Extension Request not incorporated into construction plans; or SER number, approval date, and AW project number are absent from the plan set

WWP-47.1.deficiency: Water Benchmarking Application not submitted to Austin Water or AW approval not obtained as a condition of site plan approval per LDC § 25-9-413. The Water Benchmarking Application is required for all sites with multi-family, mixed use, or commercial buildings that receive retail water service from Austin Water; one- and two-family residential sites are excluded per LDC § 25-9-410.

WWP-47.2.deficiency: For project with total gross floor area of 250,000 square feet or more (across all buildings and all phases on the same site plan or phased plan): mandatory meeting with Austin Water director to discuss Water Benchmarking Application results not held prior to site plan release. A Large Development Project is defined as one or more multi-family (5+ units), mixed use, or commercial buildings with total GFA ≥ 250,000 SF.

WWP-47.3.deficiency: On-Site Water Reuse System (OWRS) application not submitted in conjunction with the site plan permit application, or completed Water Balance Calculator (WBC) not emailed to AW_Onsitereuse@austintexas.gov for review, approval, and signature. OWRS is mandatory for Large Development Projects (total GFA ≥ 250,000 SF; multi-family, mixed use, or commercial buildings) with site plan applications filed on or after April 1, 2024, unless a director-approved fee-in-lieu or affordable housing exemption applies (LDC § 25-9-414). OWRS may also be voluntarily proposed on smaller projects.

WWP-47.4.deficiency: OWRS Meter Demand Sheet not submitted to AW_Onsitereuse@austintexas.gov for review and approval prior to site plan approval.

WWP-47.5.deficiency: Reclaimed water service requirements not confirmed with Austin Water Reclaimed Water Service Group prior to finalizing utility design.

WWP-47.6.deficiency: Coordinated approval signatures from Austin Water (AW), Reclaimed Water (RW), and On-Site Water Reuse Systems (OWRS) not obtained on the plan set when all three services are applicable.

WWP-47.7.deficiency: Austin Water main assignments not coordinated with the Austin Utility Location and Coordination Committee (AULCC) per UCM 2.9.1.B.1 and UCM 3.2.0. AULCC review is required when: (1) the project proposes water, reclaimed water, or wastewater main work in city streets (regardless of length, per UCM 2.9.1.B.1); (2) total proposed utility work in public ROW exceeds 300 LF citywide; (3) total proposed utility work in the DAPCZ exceeds 25 LF; or (4) any utility pole relocation in ROW is proposed. The AULCC issues a Completeness Letter confirming coordination is complete; this letter reference must appear on the cover sheet.

WWP-47.8.deficiency: Physical paper copies of the utility plan set (11" × 17" or 12" × 18" scale) not delivered to Austin Water at least two weeks before the scheduled AULCC meeting date.

WWP-47.9.deficiency: Industrial Waste program approval not obtained before Austin Water sign-off. Projects generating industrial waste — any commercial, retail, office, restaurant, food service, institutional, hotel, medical, laboratory, manufacturing, or governmental use discharging non-domestic wastewater to the sanitary sewer — require an Industrial Waste Discharge Permit (IWDP) under Code § 15-10-91.

WWP-47.10.deficiency: TxDOT approval not obtained before Austin Water sign-off when utility improvements are proposed within a TxDOT right-of-way. TxDOT-maintained roadways in Austin include Interstate Highways (IH-35), US Highways (US 183, US 290), State Highways (SH 71), Farm-to-Market roads (FM 2222, FM 969, etc.), and Loop 1/MoPac. Work within TxDOT ROW requires a TxDOT encroachment/utility installation permit; the permit number and roadway stationing must appear on the plan cover sheet.

WWP-47.11.deficiency: LCRA Letters of Approval or Acknowledgement not obtained for proposed wastewater mains within LCRA easement areas; letters not included in the plan submittal per Austin Water requirements. LCRA is the Lower Colorado River Authority, a Texas state agency with transmission and water management easements in the Austin area; its approval is required for any utility work within or crossing LCRA-held easement corridors.

WWP-47.12.deficiency: Building plumbing plans not reviewed for pretreatment concerns by the City of Austin when project is located within city limits and generates industrial or high-strength waste.

WWP-47.13.deficiency: Storm sewer improvements proposed in the public right-of-way without compliance with the Austin Utility Location and Coordination Committee (AULCC) review process.

WWP-47.14.deficiency: Correct Austin Water Pressure Zone designation for the subject property not verified with Austin Water and not shown on the utility plans. A pressure zone is a geographically bounded segment of AW's distribution system managed as a hydraulic unit; zone designation is authoritative in AW GIS records and cannot be independently verified from plan documents alone.

WWP-47.15.deficiency: Utility plans do not delineate which segments of proposed water and wastewater lines are public versus private to verify compliance with Chapter 15-10 of the Austin City Code.

WWP-47.16.deficiency: Existing Conditions plan sheet does not delineate which segments of existing water and wastewater lines are public versus private to verify compliance with Chapter 15-10 of the Austin City Code.

WWP-47.17.deficiency: All existing and proposed water and wastewater lines not shown on the utility plans in accordance with Austin Water Utility Standard Specifications.

WWP-47.18.deficiency: Locations of all water line services and 6-inch wastewater house connections not verified against City of Austin tap records; plan not revised to reflect actual recorded locations.

WWP-47.19.deficiency: Location, size, and material of all existing water and wastewater infrastructure not verified against City of Austin GIS records and as-built drawings; plans not corrected to match verified conditions per UCM 2.5.1.E.10. GIS numbers of all existing mains and appurtenances are required on plans per UCM 2.5.1.E.8.

WWP-47.20.deficiency: Austin Water Infrastructure Information table not completed for all existing AW utilities within or adjacent to the project area per UCM 2.1.0 and UCM 2.9.1 utility coordination criteria.

WWP-47.21.deficiency: For project indicating additions to an existing building: utility plan showing connections to the City of Austin water and wastewater system not provided.

WWP-47.22.deficiency: When Austin Water public infrastructure is proposed under a private driveway: geotechnical report for pavement design demonstrating the private drive meets City of Austin pavement design standards to protect the public infrastructure not provided.

WWP-47.23.deficiency: Current plumbing schedule not included on the plans per City Code § 15-10-31(E) and § 15-10-33(A).

WWP-47.24.deficiency: WSFU and GPM demand data for irrigation meters not provided or not confirmed as compliant by Austin Water Site Plan Plumbing review; for meters ≥ 3 inches, pipe and meter size must be determined by a Licensed Engineer Registered in the State of Texas per UCM 2.9.2.F.4.b.

WWP-47.25.deficiency: Completed meter sizing sheet not submitted to AW_ONSITEREUSE@austintexas.gov for review and approval before finalizing plans.

WWP-47.26.deficiency: If future project phases may require irrigation service from the requested meter: confirmation from Austin Water that the same meter can serve future phases not obtained, and all phased demand not shown in the meter sizing sheet.

WWP-47.27.deficiency: Whether each structure will be served by individual meters and connections or by shared common metering and infrastructure not confirmed with Austin Water.

WWP-47.28.deficiency: Irrigation meter exemption per UCM 2.9.2.F.2.b claimed without a formal waiver application on an AW-approved form and written Austin Water approval submitted; commercial and multi-family properties must purchase and install a separate AW meter for all common areas and outdoor purposes including irrigation per UCM 2.9.2.F.2.a.

WWP-47.29.deficiency: New water meters, meter boxes, and/or meter box lids not specified to conform to Austin Water's Automated Metering Infrastructure (AMI) technology and the applicable Standard Products List (SPL) per UCM 2.9.2.F.6; or site plan does not acknowledge applicant's obligation to extend AMI Data Collection Unit (DCU) infrastructure (easement to City, poles/structures for DCUs, and electrical service) to the tract. All three components — meter, box, and lid — must be on the SPL.

WWP-47.30.deficiency: Written Austin Water approval not obtained for crossing clearances between proposed utilities and AW infrastructure that do not meet UCM 2.9.1.B separation requirements.

WWP-47.31.deficiency: Waivers for horizontal separation deviations from Austin Water infrastructure requirements per UCM 2.9.1.B.2 not obtained from Austin Water before construction can proceed; deviations from the 5-foot minimum horizontal separation must be submitted in writing before final engineering plans and approved only in writing by the AW Director or designee per UCM 2.9.6.

WWP-47.32.deficiency: Proposed utility relocations not documented with all locations, sizes, and materials reviewed and approved by Austin Water Pipeline Engineering for compliance with minimum separation distances and clearance requirements prior to construction.

WWP-47.33.deficiency: Proposed telecom lines not shown on plans along indicated alignments with documentation demonstrating compliance with the 5-foot minimum horizontal separation requirement from Austin Water infrastructure per UCM 2.9.1.B.2.

WWP-47.34.deficiency: Water line encasement proposed near storm drains without coordination with and approval from the Watershed Protection Department (WPD) closed conduit maintenance team, in addition to standard Austin Water approvals.

WWP-47.35.deficiency: Complex utility crossing configurations not coordinated with Austin Water to verify compliance with all vertical separation, horizontal separation, and encasement requirements of UCM 2.9.1.B; for water or reclaimed water mains crossing under existing wastewater mains, steel encasement ≥ 18 feet centered on the wastewater main (full-circumferential welded joints) is required — no other encasement form is permitted for this crossing type.

WWP-47.36.deficiency: Root barriers not shown or not designed per UCM 2.9.1.C where street trees in the ROW planting zone are adjacent to proposed Austin Water mains or services: root barriers must be placed on all sides of the planting zone, installed no closer than 7 feet from the tree trunk; utilities must be placed no closer than 2 feet from the root barrier; and the street tree utility gap between adjacent planting zones must be a minimum of 8 feet wide between root barriers.

WWP-47.37.deficiency: Concrete thrust blocking proposed without explicit written Austin Water approval on a case-by-case basis per UCM 2.9.2.B.9; thrust block dimensions, locations, and proximity to other utilities and structures not shown on plans.

WWP-47.38.deficiency: Concrete thrust blocks proposed within the downtown area bounded by Loop 1 to IH-35 (east–west) and Lady Bird Lake to 30th Street (north–south), where concrete thrust blocking is outright prohibited under UCM 2.9.2.B.9 and UCM 2.9.3.B.11. This is an absolute prohibition — no case-by-case approval is available in this area; the design must use a mechanical restraint alternative. Note: this prohibition area is distinct from and smaller than the DAPCZ.

WWP-47.39.deficiency: "One Sided Shut Down CCT" (cut, cap, and tie-in) encasement not approved by Austin Water's Water Protection Department prior to installation, and/or photo documentation before, during, and after encasement installation not required per Austin Water standard procedures. Note: "CCT encasement" is an AW operational field term not codified in the UCM; the code-required encasement for water/reclaimed crossing under wastewater is steel encasement per UCM 2.9.1.B.3 — no other form is permitted for that crossing type. If plans call out CCT encasement at a water-under-wastewater crossing, flag for AW engineer review.

WWP-47.40.deficiency: Private well on site not identified on plans with indication of whether it will be abandoned or remain in use with proper backflow prevention; Austin Fire Department approval and written Austin Water Water Wells Program approval not obtained prior to site plan approval.

WWP-49.1.deficiency: Gravity wastewater collection pipes must not use pressure-rated PVC (AWWA C900 or ASTM D2241); gravity-rated pipe conforming to ASTM D3034 (6–15 inch, SDR-26 or less) or ASTM F679 (18–27 inch, minimum pipe stiffness PS 72) must be specified; SDR-35 PVC is never acceptable in Austin's gravity wastewater system regardless of depth or soil conditions.

WWP-49.2.deficiency: PVC gravity sewer pipe 6–15 inches in diameter must conform to ASTM D3034 with SDR 26, SDR 23.5, or a smaller SDR value; pipe marking must read "SDR-__ PVC Sewer Pipe."

WWP-49.3.deficiency: The SDR designation must be explicitly shown on all wastewater pipe material callouts and specifications to distinguish gravity-rated pipe from prohibited pressure-rated PVC; a callout of "PVC sewer pipe" without an SDR number is not acceptable.

WWP-49.4.deficiency: SDR-26 wastewater pipe at deep installations or adverse soil conditions must be evaluated for adequacy; SDR-23.5 or SDR-21 may be required based on actual depth of cover and soil loads per the SSM 510.2(l) allowable depth-of-cover tables for PVC sewer pipe.

WWP-49.5.deficiency: Private wastewater piping must not use ductile iron; an approved gravity wastewater material from Austin Water's Standard Products List must be specified.

WWP-49.6.deficiency: Wastewater gravity collection pipe, manhole, and service line materials must conform to Austin Water's Standard Products List (SPL WW-227 for ASTM D3034 PVC sewer pipe; SPL WW-227A for ASTM F679 PVC sewer pipe; SPL WW-227B for fittings).

WWP-49.7.deficiency: Connection to existing concrete wastewater service lines is not permitted; a new wastewater service line must be designed using materials conforming to Austin Water's Standard Products List.

WWP-49.8.deficiency: Private wastewater service lines must not exceed 10-inch diameter.

WWP-49.9.deficiency: Wastewater force mains outside the lift station site must use high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipe and fittings; plans specifying ductile iron, PVC (including "Yelomine" or locked push-on D2241 PVC), or any other material for force main pipe outside the lift station site are non-compliant unless accompanied by documented Austin Water approval for an alternative material. The former UCM 2.9.4.B diameter-based split (HDPE/Yelomine ≤6-inch; PE >6-inch) is obsolete and no longer applies. Note: SSM 510.2(8) states force mains shall be DI, which conflicts with the current UCM — the UCM governs as the primary design standard.

WWP-49.10.deficiency: At all connections between HDPE wastewater force main pipe and valves or ductile iron fittings, HDPE mechanical joint (MJ) adaptors per AW SPL WW-706A must be specified; non-standard connection methods or fittings not listed on SPL WW-706A are not permitted at these transition points.

WWP-49.11.deficiency: Where wastewater force mains transition from HDPE pipe to a different pipe material (ductile iron, PVC, etc.), the HDPE pipe segments must be designed to undergo isolated hydrostatic testing separately from the non-HDPE segments, via isolation valves or other isolation means shown on plans.

WWP-49.12.deficiency: Connector type must match pipe size per Austin Water standard practice: 2-inch service taps require no adapter; 4-inch connections require Foster adapters; 6–8-inch connections require swivel tees; connections larger than 8 inches require Foster adapters; all inline gate valves require Foster adapters. The Foster adapter and swivel tee specifications are not reproduced in Bureau regulatory codes — reviewers must reference current Austin Water standard practice.

WWP-49.13.deficiency: Mechanical water service clamps are permitted only for connections to HDPE pipe (per SPL WW-264); for connections to HDPE pipe, electrofusion saddles per SPL WW-706C are also acceptable; connections to DI, PVC, or AC pipe must use saddle taps per applicable COA Standard Detail.

WWP-49.14.deficiency: Tapping sleeves and tapping valves for pressure taps must be selected from Austin Water's Standard Products List; reduced-wall resilient-seated gate valves (including tapping valves) shall conform to AWWA C515 and SPL WW-700; tapping sleeve material and detail must match COA Standard Detail 520-AW-04.

WWP-49.15.deficiency: All break-away fittings must be on Austin Water's Standard Products List; Models 1220 and 2020 are not approved and must be replaced with SPL-approved models.

WWP-49.16.deficiency: All pipe fittings must be selected from Austin Water's Standard Products List; non-standard fittings not on the SPL must include manufacturer specification sheets documenting compliance, or be replaced with SPL-approved fittings.

WWP-49.17.deficiency: One-Sided Shut Down (CCT) encasement must be installed on water service lines between the water service connection (immediately downstream of the meter) and the water line entry into the building.

WWP-49.18.deficiency: CCT encasement must extend vertically from the pipe centerline to a minimum of 6 inches above the top of the pipe, and horizontally a minimum of 2 times the pipe diameter.

WWP-49.19.deficiency: CCT encasement material must be approved concrete or flowable fill; the encasement material must be identified on plans.

WWP-49.20.deficiency: Underground detectable tape labeled "Caution Buried Water Line Below" must be installed within 12 inches of the top of the flowable fill.

WWP-49.21.deficiency: Pipe must be covered with plastic sheeting or equivalent before placement of CCT or concrete encasement.

WWP-49.22.deficiency: Water lines installed below non-Austin Water utility infrastructure (storm drain, gas, etc.) require steel encasement when vertical separation is less than the minimum required: 18 inches when water/reclaimed/wastewater mains are below non-AW infrastructure (reduced to 12 inches only with AW approval); 12 inches when above non-AW infrastructure (reduced to 6 inches only with AW approval).

WWP-49.23.deficiency: All new water meters must be compatible with Austin Water's Automated Metering Infrastructure (AMI) technology; AMI compliance requires that meters, meter boxes, and meter box lids all conform to the AW AMI system and the applicable SPL — a common error is specifying AMI-compatible meters but using non-approved lids.

WWP-49.24.deficiency: Water meters must be the Sensus brand or otherwise selected from Austin Water's Standard Products List; generic meter designations such as "water meter per AW" without confirmed SPL identification are not acceptable.

WWP-49.25.deficiency: Fire line water meters must be specified as "Meter (512-AW-02)" per Austin Water's Standard Products List.

WWP-49.26.deficiency: New reclaimed water meters, meter boxes, and meter box lids must conform to Austin Water's AMI technology requirements and the applicable SPL; the same AMI extension cost responsibilities (DCU infrastructure, easements) apply to reclaimed water meters as to potable water meters.

WWP-49.27.deficiency: Plans must include a general note stating: "Piping materials and appurtenances shall conform to COA Standard Specifications and Austin Water's Standard Products List (SPL)." Plans without this note are deficient regardless of whether individual materials are otherwise correctly specified.

WWP-49.28.deficiency: Material callouts on plans must include the Austin Water SPL number (e.g., "SPL WW-65" for HDPE service tubing, "SPL WW-227" for PVC sewer pipe, "SPL WW-706A" for HDPE force main MJ adaptors); callouts that identify material type only without SPL numbers require verification against the current AW SPL document.

WWP-49.29.deficiency: Hydraulic C-factors used in calculations must match Austin Water specifications: C-factor of 80 for ductile iron pipe (both unlined and cement-lined) and C-factor of 110 for all plastic pipe (PVC, HDPE, and copper) per FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2. A higher C-coefficient may be used for new mains only upon AW approval with sufficient documentation showing effects of long-term use; plans using C=150 or C=130 for DI without AW approval are non-compliant.

WWP-49.30.deficiency: Plans must use correct COA standard terminology; non-standard terms (e.g., "TAP VALVE") must be replaced with approved Austin Water terminology.

WWP-49.31.deficiency: Gate valve symbols on plans must conform to COA standard drawing symbols per Austin Water requirements.

WWP-49.32.deficiency: Water line trench specifications must reference the current Austin Water General Information and Construction Notes Sheets; custom trench notes that do not fully comply with all standard requirements or that fail to incorporate the current standard AW Construction Notes are not acceptable.

WWP-49.33.deficiency: All Austin Water appurtenances (valve boxes, meter boxes, fire hydrant access points, air valve assemblies) must be protected from being paved or concreted over during pavement restoration; this requirement must be addressed on plans.

WWP-49.34.deficiency: Water vault sizes must conform to Austin Water's Standard Products List and applicable standard details.

WWP-49.35.deficiency: The existing water main pipe material must be verified against Austin Water records at all proposed connection points; the verified material governs replacement and restraint requirements; plans must include a note confirming that existing pipe material was verified against AW records prior to design.
